geo33-advanced-p04.stemHtml: Three concentric circles have radii , and , where . The smallest disk and the region outside the middle circle but inside the largest circle are shaded. What is the total shaded area?
explanation: The small disk has area $\pi a^2$. The outer ring has area $\pi(3c)^2-\pi(2b)^2=9\pi c^2-4\pi b^2$. Adding gives $\pi(9c^2-4b^2+a^2)$.
geo33-advanced-p04.answerHtml: The small disk has area . The outer ring has area . Adding gives .

methods.title: Add the disk and the outer ring
steps: The small disk has area $\pi a^2$. The outer ring has area $\pi(3c)^2-\pi(2b)^2=9\pi c^2-4\pi b^2$. Adding gives $\pi(9c^2-4b^2+a^2)$.

methods.title: Remove the only white region from the largest disk
steps: The largest area is $9\pi c^2$. The white ring between radii a and 2b has area $4\pi b^2-\pi a^2$. Subtract the entire bracket to obtain $9\pi c^2-4\pi b^2+\pi a^2$.

geo33-advanced-p05.stemRich: A, B, C and D lie on a circle. Given: angle CAD is 44°, angle CDB is 24°, and angle ADB equals angle ABD. What is angle ABD?
geo33-advanced-p05.stemHtml: A, B, C and D lie on a circle. Given: angle CAD is 44°, angle CDB is 24°, and angle ADB equals angle ABD. What is angle ABD?
explanation: Angles ABD and ACD intercept the same arc AD, so both equal α. Angle ADC is α+24°. Triangle ACD gives 44°+α+(α+24°)=180°, so α=56°.
geo33-advanced-p05.answerHtml: Angles ABD and ACD intercept the same arc AD, so both equal α. Angle ADC is α+24°. Triangle ACD gives 44°+α+(α+24°)=180°, so α=56°.

methods.title: Transfer an inscribed angle into triangle ACD
steps: Angles ABD and ACD intercept the same arc AD, so both equal α. Angle ADC is α+24°. Triangle ACD gives 44°+α+(α+24°)=180°, so α=56°.

methods.title: Add the arc measures
steps: Arc CD measures 88° and arc CB 48°. Equal angles ADB and ABD give equal arcs AB and AD. Those two arcs share the remaining 224°, so each is 112°. The requested inscribed angle is half 112°, or 56°.

geo33-advanced-p07.stem: Four semicircular arcs have radii whose average is m. What is the sum of the lengths of the four curved arcs?
geo33-advanced-p07.stemRich: Four semicircular arcs have radii whose average is m. What is the sum of the lengths of the four curved arcs?
geo33-advanced-p07.stemHtml: Four semicircular arcs have radii whose average is m. What is the sum of the lengths of the four curved arcs?
explanation: A semicircular arc of radius r has length πr. The four radii sum to 4m, so the total curved length is π×4m=4πm.
geo33-advanced-p07.answerHtml: A semicircular arc of radius r has length πr. The four radii sum to 4m, so the total curved length is π×4m=4πm.

methods.title: Use the sum supplied by the mean
steps: A semicircular arc of radius r has length πr. The four radii sum to 4m, so the total curved length is π×4m=4πm.

methods.title: Balance the radii around their mean
steps: Arc length changes linearly with radius. Replacing the four radii by their common average m keeps the sum of arc lengths unchanged. Four arcs of radius m each have length πm, for total 4πm.

geo33-advanced-p08.stemRich: A circular garden has radius 600 m. A path 100 m wide is built around its entire outside edge. What is the area of the path (in km²)?
geo33-advanced-p08.stemHtml: A circular garden has radius 600 m. A path 100 m wide is built around its entire outside edge. What is the area of the path (in km²)?
explanation: The inner radius is 0.6 km and the outer radius 0.7 km. The path area is π(0.7²−0.6²)=π(0.49−0.36)=0.13π km².
geo33-advanced-p08.answerHtml: The inner radius is 0.6 km and the outer radius 0.7 km. The path area is π(0.7²−0.6²)=π(0.49−0.36)=0.13π km².

methods.title: Convert the radii to kilometers first
steps: The inner radius is 0.6 km and the outer radius 0.7 km. The path area is π(0.7²−0.6²)=π(0.49−0.36)=0.13π km².

methods.title: Calculate in square meters, then convert
steps: The area is π(700²−600²)=130000π m². One square kilometer is 1000000 m², so the area is 0.13π km².

methods.title: Factor the difference of squares
steps: In kilometers, the radius difference is 0.1 and the sum is 1.3. The ring area is π×0.1×1.3=0.13π.

geo33-advanced-p09.stemHtml: A sector has central angle 150°. Its area, measured in cm², is numerically 3 times as much as its arc length, measured in cm. What is the radius of its circle (in cm)?
explanation: Let f=150:360. The given numerical equality is fπr²=3(f×2πr). Cancel the positive factors f,π and r to obtain r=6.
geo33-advanced-p09.answerHtml: Let f=150:360. The given numerical equality is fπr²=3(f×2πr). Cancel the positive factors f,π and r to obtain r=6.

methods.title: Cancel the common sector fraction
steps: Let f=150:360. The given numerical equality is fπr²=3(f×2πr). Cancel the positive factors f,π and r to obtain r=6.

methods.title: Use the area-to-arc relationship
steps: A sector’s area equals one half of its radius times its arc length, because both use the same fraction of a circle. Therefore the numerical area-to-arc ratio is r:2. Set r:2=3, giving r=6.

methods.title: Use bounds instead of a rounded result
steps: Since 3.14<π<22:7, the removed area lies between 14.13 and 99:7. Thus the remainder lies between 153:7≈21.857 and 21.87, placing it strictly between 21 and 22.

geo33-advanced-p13.stemHtml: AB is a diameter of a circle with radius 5 cm. C lies on one semicircular arc AB. Arc CB is twice as long as arc AC. What is BC (in cm)?

methods.title: Find the inscribed angles
steps: The semicircle is divided into 60° arc AC and 120° arc CB. The triangle’s angles at B and A are 30° and 60°, and C is 90°. With hypotenuse AB=10, the longer leg BC is 5√3.

methods.title: Use the central isosceles triangle
steps: Central angle BOC is 120°. Its altitude to chord BC splits it into two 30°–60°–90° triangles with hypotenuse 5. Each half-chord is 5√3:2, so the full chord is 5√3.

geo33-advanced-p15.stem: Four circles have centers A, B, C and D. Each is externally tangent to its two neighbors in the order A, B, C, D, A. Given: AB=6 cm, BC=10 cm, and CD=14 cm. What is AD (in cm)?
geo33-advanced-p15.stemRich: Four circles have centers A, B, C and D. Each is externally tangent to its two neighbors in the order A, B, C, D, A. Given: $AB=6$ cm, $BC=10$ cm, and $CD=14$ cm. What is AD (in cm)?
geo33-advanced-p15.stemHtml: Four circles have centers A, B, C and D. Each is externally tangent to its two neighbors in the order A, B, C, D, A. Given: cm, cm, and cm. What is AD (in cm)?
explanation: Write the radii as a, b, c, d. Then AB+CD=(a+b)+(c+d), while BC+AD=(b+c)+(a+d); both equal the sum of all four radii. Thus 6+14=10+AD, giving AD=10.
geo33-advanced-p15.answerHtml: Write the radii as a, b, c, d. Then AB+CD=(a+b)+(c+d), while BC+AD=(b+c)+(a+d); both equal the sum of all four radii. Thus 6+14=10+AD, giving AD=10.

methods.title: Use the sum of the four radii
steps: Write the radii as a, b, c, d. Then AB+CD=(a+b)+(c+d), while BC+AD=(b+c)+(a+d); both equal the sum of all four radii. Thus 6+14=10+AD, giving AD=10.

methods.title: Track radius differences
steps: BC−AB=c−a=4. Also CD−AD=c−a=4. Therefore AD=CD−4=14−4=10. The actual individual radii are unnecessary.

steps: All boundary arcs belong to congruent circles, so their lengths can be combined by adding their central angles. The three triangle angles sum to 180°. Half of circumference 12π is 6π.

geo33-advanced-p17.stem: Square ABCD is inscribed in a circle with circumference 12\pi cm. E, F, G and H are the midpoints of its sides. What is the area of square EFGH (in cm²)?
geo33-advanced-p17.stemRich: Square ABCD is inscribed in a circle with circumference $12\pi$ cm. E, F, G and H are the midpoints of its sides. What is the area of square EFGH (in cm²)?
geo33-advanced-p17.stemHtml: Square ABCD is inscribed in a circle with circumference cm. E, F, G and H are the midpoints of its sides. What is the area of square EFGH (in cm²)?
explanation: The circle diameter is 12, which is a diagonal of ABCD. The outer square area is 12²:2=72. Joining its side midpoints produces a square of half that area,36.
geo33-advanced-p17.answerHtml: The circle diameter is 12, which is a diagonal of ABCD. The outer square area is 12²:2=72. Joining its side midpoints produces a square of half that area,36.

methods.title: Take half the outer square’s area
steps: The circle diameter is 12, which is a diagonal of ABCD. The outer square area is 12²:2=72. Joining its side midpoints produces a square of half that area,36.

methods.title: Use a triangle midsegment
steps: EH joins the midpoints of two sides of triangle ABD, so EH is half diagonal BD. BD=12, hence EH=6 and the inner square area is 6²=36.

methods.title: Use two right-isosceles side relationships
steps: The outer side is 12:√2=6√2. Each corner half-side is 3√2. The inner side is its right-isosceles hypotenuse,3√2×√2=6, giving area 36.

geo33-advanced-p18.stemRich: A circle with center O has radius 4 cm. A and E lie on the circle, angle AOE is 45°, and B is the foot of the perpendicular from A to OE. What is the area of sector AOE outside triangle AOB (in cm²)?
geo33-advanced-p18.stemHtml: A circle with center O has radius 4 cm. A and E lie on the circle, angle AOE is 45°, and B is the foot of the perpendicular from A to OE. What is the area of sector AOE outside triangle AOB (in cm²)?
explanation: The 45° sector has area 16π:8=2π. Triangle AOB is right and isosceles with hypotenuse OA=4, so its legs are 2√2 and its area is 4. The difference is 2π−4.
geo33-advanced-p18.answerHtml: The 45° sector has area 16π:8=2π. Triangle AOB is right and isosceles with hypotenuse OA=4, so its legs are 2√2 and its area is 4. The difference is 2π−4.

methods.title: Subtract the right triangle from the sector
steps: The 45° sector has area 16π:8=2π. Triangle AOB is right and isosceles with hypotenuse OA=4, so its legs are 2√2 and its area is 4. The difference is 2π−4.

methods.title: Find the triangle area from its hypotenuse
steps: For a right isosceles triangle, the sum of the two equal leg squares is the hypotenuse square 16. Each leg square is 8, and half the product of the equal legs is 4. Subtract 4 from the sector area 2π.

methods.title: Eliminate impossible area expressions
steps: The target area is positive and smaller than its sector area 2π. Both π−4 and 2π−8 are negative because π<4. To distinguish the remaining choices, the exact triangle area 4 gives 2π−4; a rough visual comparison alone is insufficient.

geo33-advanced-p19.stemRich: ABCD is a trapezoid with $AD\parallel BC$, circumscribed about a circle with center O and radius 6 cm. The circle is tangent to CD at E and to BC at F. Given: angle ADC is 60°. What is the area of the minor sector EOF (in cm²)?
geo33-advanced-p19.stemHtml: ABCD is a trapezoid with , circumscribed about a circle with center O and radius 6 cm. The circle is tangent to CD at E and to BC at F. Given: angle ADC is 60°. What is the area of the minor sector EOF (in cm²)?
explanation: Parallel AD and BC make angle ECF=120°. Radii OE and OF are perpendicular to their tangents, so quadrilateral OECF has two right angles. Hence EOF=360°−120°−180°=60°. The sector area is 36π:6=6π.
geo33-advanced-p19.answerHtml: Parallel AD and BC make angle ECF=120°. Radii OE and OF are perpendicular to their tangents, so quadrilateral OECF has two right angles. Hence EOF=360°−120°−180°=60°. The sector area is 36π:6=6π.

methods.title: Use the tangent quadrilateral
steps: Parallel AD and BC make angle ECF=120°. Radii OE and OF are perpendicular to their tangents, so quadrilateral OECF has two right angles. Hence EOF=360°−120°−180°=60°. The sector area is 36π:6=6π.

methods.title: Compare angles between perpendicular lines
steps: OE is perpendicular to CD, and OF is perpendicular to BC, which is parallel to AD. The smaller angle between the radii therefore equals the 60° angle between CD and AD. It takes one sixth of the radius 6 disk, giving 6π.

geo33-advanced-p20.stem: Two externally tangent circles with centers A and B have radii 9 cm and 4 cm. A common tangent touches them at D and C, respectively. What is the perimeter of quadrilateral ABCD (in cm)?
geo33-advanced-p20.stemRich: Two externally tangent circles with centers A and B have radii 9 cm and 4 cm. A common tangent touches them at D and C, respectively. What is the perimeter of quadrilateral ABCD (in cm)?
geo33-advanced-p20.stemHtml: Two externally tangent circles with centers A and B have radii 9 cm and 4 cm. A common tangent touches them at D and C, respectively. What is the perimeter of quadrilateral ABCD (in cm)?
explanation: AB=9+4=13. The centers differ in height by 9−4=5 above the common tangent. Their horizontal separation DC is therefore √(13²−5²)=12. The perimeter is 13+4+12+9=38.
geo33-advanced-p20.answerHtml: AB=9+4=13. The centers differ in height by 9−4=5 above the common tangent. Their horizontal separation DC is therefore √(13²−5²)=12. The perimeter is 13+4+12+9=38.

methods.title: Use the radius sum and a right triangle
steps: AB=9+4=13. The centers differ in height by 9−4=5 above the common tangent. Their horizontal separation DC is therefore √(13²−5²)=12. The perimeter is 13+4+12+9=38.

methods.title: Use the common-tangent length formula, derived by factoring
steps: DC²=(R+r)²−(R−r)²=4 Rr. For R=9 and r=4, DC=2√36=12. Add the two radii and center distance 13:12+9+4+13=38.

explanation: The perpendicular distance from the common center to the chord is the small radius 5. Half the chord is √(13²−5²)=12, so the whole chord is 24.

methods.title: Recognise the 5–12–13 triangle
steps: A radius to the tangency point is perpendicular to the chord and bisects it. Each half forms a right triangle with leg 5 and hypotenuse 13, so the other leg is 12 and the full chord 24.

methods.title: Use meters throughout

geo33-advanced-p23.stemHtml: Three circles of radius 2 cm are pairwise externally tangent. What is the area of the region between them enclosed by the three minor arcs joining their tangency points (in cm²)?
explanation: The centers form an equilateral triangle of side 4 and area 4√3. Each circle contributes a60° sector inside this triangle. The three sectors together make half a radius 2 disk, with area 2π. The gap is 4√3−2π.

methods.title: Calculate one third of the gap
steps: The triangle’s three symmetric portions each have area 4√3:3 and contain a sector of area 2π:3. One gap portion is (4√3−2π):3; multiplying by 3 gives 4√3−2π.

geo33-advanced-p24.stemRich: The area between two concentric circles is $45\pi$ cm². Their radii differ by 3 cm. What is the smaller radius (in cm)?
geo33-advanced-p24.stemHtml: The area between two concentric circles is cm². Their radii differ by 3 cm. What is the smaller radius (in cm)?
explanation: R²−r²=45 and R−r=3. Thus(R−r)(R+r)=45 gives R+r=15. The smaller radius is (15−3):2=6.
geo33-advanced-p24.answerHtml: R²−r²=45 and R−r=3. Thus(R−r)(R+r)=45 gives R+r=15. The smaller radius is (15−3):2=6.

methods.title: Factor a difference of squares
steps: R²−r²=45 and R−r=3. Thus(R−r)(R+r)=45 gives R+r=15. The smaller radius is (15−3):2=6.

methods.title: Use one variable
steps: Let the small radius be r and the large one r+3. Then(r+3)²−r²=45, so 6r+9=45 and r=6.

geo33-advanced-p25.stemRich: A rectangle with sides 10 cm and 24 cm is inscribed in a circle. What is the area of the circle (in cm²)?
geo33-advanced-p25.stemHtml: A rectangle with sides 10 cm and 24 cm is inscribed in a circle. What is the area of the circle (in cm²)?
explanation: The diagonal is √(10²+24²)=26. It is a circle diameter, so the radius is 13 and the area 169π.
geo33-advanced-p25.answerHtml: The diagonal is √(10²+24²)=26. It is a circle diameter, so the radius is 13 and the area 169π.

methods.title: Find the rectangle diagonal
steps: The diagonal is √(10²+24²)=26. It is a circle diameter, so the radius is 13 and the area 169π.

methods.title: Work with half the rectangle
steps: From the rectangle center to a vertex, the horizontal and vertical distances are 12 and 5. This 5–12–13 right triangle has hypotenuse equal to the circle radius 13, again giving 169π.

geo33-advanced-p26.stem: A circle is inscribed in a right triangle whose legs are 6 cm and 8 cm. What is the circle’s radius (in cm)?
geo33-advanced-p26.stemRich: A circle is inscribed in a right triangle whose legs are 6 cm and 8 cm. What is the circle’s radius (in cm)?
geo33-advanced-p26.stemHtml: A circle is inscribed in a right triangle whose legs are 6 cm and 8 cm. What is the circle’s radius (in cm)?
explanation: The hypotenuse is 10. From the right-angle vertex, each tangency distance equals r. The other tangent lengths along the legs are 6−r and 8−r, and together they make the hypotenuse 10. Thus 14−2r=10 and r=2.
geo33-advanced-p26.answerHtml: The hypotenuse is 10. From the right-angle vertex, each tangency distance equals r. The other tangent lengths along the legs are 6−r and 8−r, and together they make the hypotenuse 10. Thus 14−2r=10 and r=2.

methods.title: Use equal tangent segments
steps: The hypotenuse is 10. From the right-angle vertex, each tangency distance equals r. The other tangent lengths along the legs are 6−r and 8−r, and together they make the hypotenuse 10. Thus 14−2r=10 and r=2.

methods.title: Split the triangle into three triangles with height r
steps: The triangle area is 6×8:2=24. Joining the incenter to all vertices divides it into triangles whose bases sum to the perimeter 24 and whose heights are all r. Their total area is 24r:2=12r. Therefore r=2.

geo33-advanced-p27.stem: Two circles have radius 4 cm, and the distance between their centers is 4 cm. What is the area common to both disks (in cm²)?
geo33-advanced-p27.stemRich: Two circles have radius 4 cm, and the distance between their centers is 4 cm. What is the area common to both disks (in cm²)?
geo33-advanced-p27.stemHtml: Two circles have radius 4 cm, and the distance between their centers is 4 cm. What is the area common to both disks (in cm²)?
explanation: Joining each intersection to both centers creates two equilateral triangles of side 4. Each minor central angle between the intersections is 120°. One segment has area (1:3)×16π minus the isosceles triangle area 4√3. Doubling gives 32π:3−8√3.
geo33-advanced-p27.answerHtml: Joining each intersection to both centers creates two equilateral triangles of side 4. Each minor central angle between the intersections is 120°. One segment has area (1:3)×16π minus the isosceles triangle area 4√3. Doubling gives 32π:3−8√3.

methods.title: Add two equal circular segments
steps: Joining each intersection to both centers creates two equilateral triangles of side 4. Each minor central angle between the intersections is 120°. One segment has area (1:3)×16π minus the isosceles triangle area 4√3. Doubling gives 32π:3−8√3.

methods.title: Add the two sectors and remove the central rhombus
steps: The two 120° sectors total 32π:3. Their combined overlap beyond the required lens is the rhombus formed by the centers and intersection points. It consists of two side 4 equilateral triangles with total area 8√3. Subtract to obtain 32π:3−8√3.

explanation: The wire becomes the entire circumference. Thus $2\pi r=10$, and dividing by $2\pi$ gives $r=\frac5\pi$.

methods.title: Use the circumference formula
steps: The wire becomes the entire circumference. Thus $2\pi r=10$, and dividing by $2\pi$ gives $r=\frac5\pi$.

methods.title: Find the diameter first
steps: Circumference equals $\pi$ times diameter, so the diameter is $\frac{10}\pi$. The radius is half the diameter, giving $\frac5\pi$.

geo33-foundation-p03.stemRich: In the accompanying figure, AD is a diameter of a circle with center O, $AB\parallel CD$, and angle COD is 140°. What is angle BAD?
geo33-foundation-p03.stemHtml: In the accompanying figure, AD is a diameter of a circle with center O, , and angle COD is 140°. What is angle BAD?
explanation: OC=OD, so triangle COD has base angles (180°−140°) divided by 2=20°. Because AB is parallel to CD and AD is a transversal, angle BAD equals angle CDO, or 20°.
geo33-foundation-p03.answerHtml: OC=OD, so triangle COD has base angles (180°−140°) divided by 2=20°. Because AB is parallel to CD and AD is a transversal, angle BAD equals angle CDO, or 20°.

methods.title: Use an isosceles triangle and parallel lines
steps: OC=OD, so triangle COD has base angles (180°−140°) divided by 2=20°. Because AB is parallel to CD and AD is a transversal, angle BAD equals angle CDO, or 20°.

methods.title: Use equal arcs between parallel chords
steps: Parallel chords AB and CD cut off equal side arcs AC and BD. The diameter AD gives arc AC plus arc CD equal to 180°. Since arc CD measures 140°, arc AC and therefore arc BD each measure 40°. Inscribed angle BAD intercepts arc BD and equals 20°.

geo33-foundation-p04.stem: AB is a diameter of a circle with center O. C and D lie on the same semicircle in the order B, C, D, A. Given: angle BAC equals angle CAD. Which of the following statements is necessarily true?
geo33-foundation-p04.stemRich: AB is a diameter of a circle with center O. C and D lie on the same semicircle in the order B, C, D, A. Given: angle BAC equals angle CAD. Which of the following statements is necessarily true?
geo33-foundation-p04.stemHtml: AB is a diameter of a circle with center O. C and D lie on the same semicircle in the order B, C, D, A. Given: angle BAC equals angle CAD. Which of the following statements is necessarily true?
explanation: Equal inscribed angles BAC and CAD intercept equal arcs BC and CD. Equal arcs in the same circle have equal chords, so BC=CD.
geo33-foundation-p04.answerHtml: Equal inscribed angles BAC and CAD intercept equal arcs BC and CD. Equal arcs in the same circle have equal chords, so BC=CD.

methods.title: Use equal inscribed angles
steps: Equal inscribed angles BAC and CAD intercept equal arcs BC and CD. Equal arcs in the same circle have equal chords, so BC=CD.

methods.title: Compare the central triangles
steps: The corresponding central angles BOC and COD are equal because each is twice its inscribed angle. Triangles BOC and COD have two equal radius sides and equal included angles, so their third sides BC and CD are equal.

geo33-foundation-p05.stemHtml: Triangle ABC is inscribed in a circle of area cm². Given: cm. What is angle ABC?
explanation: The area gives r²=16, so r=4 and the diameter is 8. Chord AC has that maximum length and must be a diameter. An inscribed angle subtending a diameter is 90°.
geo33-foundation-p05.answerHtml: The area gives r²=16, so r=4 and the diameter is 8. Chord AC has that maximum length and must be a diameter. An inscribed angle subtending a diameter is 90°.

methods.title: Use the center and equal radii
steps: AO and OC each have length 4. Their sum equals AC=8, so equality in the triangle inequality puts O on AC. Thus arc AC not containing B is a semicircle, and angle ABC is half 180°, or 90°.

geo33-foundation-p07.stem: Triangle ABC is inscribed in a circle, and angle BAC is 36°. What fraction of the circumference is the major arc BC, which contains A?
geo33-foundation-p07.stemRich: Triangle ABC is inscribed in a circle, and angle BAC is 36°. What fraction of the circumference is the major arc BC, which contains A?
geo33-foundation-p07.stemHtml: Triangle ABC is inscribed in a circle, and angle BAC is 36°. What fraction of the circumference is the major arc BC, which contains A?
explanation: The minor arc BC measures 2×36°=72°, or one fifth of a full turn. The major arc is the remaining four fifths.
geo33-foundation-p07.answerHtml: The minor arc BC measures 2×36°=72°, or one fifth of a full turn. The major arc is the remaining four fifths.

methods.title: Subtract the minor-arc fraction
steps: The minor arc BC measures 2×36°=72°, or one fifth of a full turn. The major arc is the remaining four fifths.

methods.title: Calculate the major central angle
steps: The major arc measures 360°−72°=288°. Its fraction of the circumference is 288 divided by 360, which reduces to 4:5.

geo33-foundation-p09.stemRich: Circles with centers K and M intersect at A and B. MA is tangent to the circle with center K at A, and KB is tangent to the circle with center M at B. Given: angle AMB is 72°. What is angle AKB?
geo33-foundation-p09.stemHtml: Circles with centers K and M intersect at A and B. MA is tangent to the circle with center K at A, and KB is tangent to the circle with center M at B. Given: angle AMB is 72°. What is angle AKB?
explanation: The radius–tangent angles KAM and KBM are 90°. The four angles of quadrilateral KAMB total 360°. Thus AKB=360°−90°−90°−72°=108°.
geo33-foundation-p09.answerHtml: The radius–tangent angles KAM and KBM are 90°. The four angles of quadrilateral KAMB total 360°. Thus AKB=360°−90°−90°−72°=108°.

methods.title: Use the quadrilateral angle sum
steps: The radius–tangent angles KAM and KBM are 90°. The four angles of quadrilateral KAMB total 360°. Thus AKB=360°−90°−90°−72°=108°.

methods.title: Use the two right triangles around KM
steps: The two circles give KA=KB and MA=MB, so triangles KAM and KBM are congruent. KM bisects angle AMB into 36° pieces. Each right triangle then has 54° at K, giving 108° in total.

geo33-foundation-p10.stem: AB is a diameter of a circle with center O. OB is a diameter of a smaller circle whose circumference is 6\pi cm. What is the circumference of the larger circle (in cm)?
geo33-foundation-p10.stemRich: AB is a diameter of a circle with center O. OB is a diameter of a smaller circle whose circumference is $6\pi$ cm. What is the circumference of the larger circle (in cm)?
geo33-foundation-p10.stemHtml: AB is a diameter of a circle with center O. OB is a diameter of a smaller circle whose circumference is cm. What is the circumference of the larger circle (in cm)?
explanation: The small diameter is its circumference divided by π, or 6. This is the large radius. The large circumference is 2π×6=12π.
geo33-foundation-p10.answerHtml: The small diameter is its circumference divided by π, or 6. This is the large radius. The large circumference is 2π×6=12π.

methods.title: Find the large radius
steps: The small diameter is its circumference divided by π, or 6. This is the large radius. The large circumference is 2π×6=12π.

methods.title: Use the linear scale factor
steps: The large diameter is twice OB, the small diameter. Circumferences have the same 2:1 ratio as diameters, so the larger circumference is twice 6π, or 12π.

geo33-foundation-p11.stem: AB and AC are tangent to a circle with center O at B and C. The smaller central angle BOC is 144°. What is angle ABC?
geo33-foundation-p11.stemRich: AB and AC are tangent to a circle with center O at B and C. The smaller central angle BOC is 144°. What is angle ABC?
geo33-foundation-p11.stemHtml: AB and AC are tangent to a circle with center O at B and C. The smaller central angle BOC is 144°. What is angle ABC?
explanation: Triangle BOC is isosceles, with base angles (180°−144°) divided by 2=18°. At B, tangent BA is perpendicular to radius BO. The angle between BA and BC is 90°−18°=72°.
geo33-foundation-p11.answerHtml: Triangle BOC is isosceles, with base angles (180°−144°) divided by 2=18°. At B, tangent BA is perpendicular to radius BO. The angle between BA and BC is 90°−18°=72°.

methods.title: Subtract from the tangent–radius right angle
steps: Triangle BOC is isosceles, with base angles (180°−144°) divided by 2=18°. At B, tangent BA is perpendicular to radius BO. The angle between BA and BC is 90°−18°=72°.

methods.title: Use the tangent kite and the equal tangents
steps: In quadrilateral ABOC, angles B and C are 90°, so angle BAC=36°. Equal tangent segments AB and AC make triangle ABC isosceles. Each base angle is (180°−36°) divided by 2=72°.

geo33-foundation-p12.stemRich: Two congruent circles with centers A and B are externally tangent. The sum of their areas is $50\pi$ cm². What is AB (in cm)?
geo33-foundation-p12.stemHtml: Two congruent circles with centers A and B are externally tangent. The sum of their areas is cm². What is AB (in cm)?
explanation: Each disk has area 25π, so each radius is 5. Externally tangent centers are separated by the sum of the radii, giving AB=10.
geo33-foundation-p12.answerHtml: Each disk has area 25π, so each radius is 5. Externally tangent centers are separated by the sum of the radii, giving AB=10.

methods.title: Find one radius
steps: Each disk has area 25π, so each radius is 5. Externally tangent centers are separated by the sum of the radii, giving AB=10.

methods.title: Express area directly in terms of AB
steps: Each radius is AB divided by 2. Thus total area=2π(AB:2)²=πAB²:2. Equating to 50π gives AB²=100 and AB=10.

methods.title: Use symmetry and a right triangle
steps: AO bisects the isosceles vertex angle, so DAO=34°. Right triangle ADO has angle DOA=56°. The matching right triangle AEO supplies another 56°, giving DOE=112°.

geo33-foundation-p15.stem: Quadrilateral ABCD is inscribed in a circle of area 25\pi cm². Diagonal AC bisects both angle A and angle C. What is AC (in cm)?
geo33-foundation-p15.stemRich: Quadrilateral ABCD is inscribed in a circle of area $25\pi$ cm². Diagonal AC bisects both angle A and angle C. What is AC (in cm)?
geo33-foundation-p15.stemHtml: Quadrilateral ABCD is inscribed in a circle of area cm². Diagonal AC bisects both angle A and angle C. What is AC (in cm)?
explanation: Write the full opposite angles as 2α and 2β. A cyclic quadrilateral has opposite-angle sum 180°, so α+β=90°. Triangle ABC therefore has angle B=90°, making AC a diameter. The radius from area 25π is 5, so AC=10.
geo33-foundation-p15.answerHtml: Write the full opposite angles as 2α and 2β. A cyclic quadrilateral has opposite-angle sum 180°, so α+β=90°. Triangle ABC therefore has angle B=90°, making AC a diameter. The radius from area 25π is 5, so AC=10.

methods.title: Show that AC is a diameter
steps: Write the full opposite angles as 2α and 2β. A cyclic quadrilateral has opposite-angle sum 180°, so α+β=90°. Triangle ABC therefore has angle B=90°, making AC a diameter. The radius from area 25π is 5, so AC=10.

methods.title: Use equal chords and the cyclic condition
steps: The angle bisectors give AB=AD and CB=CD by equal intercepted arcs. Triangles ABC and ADC are congruent, so their opposite angles B and D are equal. They also sum to 180° in the cyclic quadrilateral, hence each is 90°. Thus AC is the diameter 10.

choices: A kite with opposite angles of 90° and 72°
An isosceles trapezoid with upper base angles of 104°

explanation: A cyclic quadrilateral must have opposite angles totaling 180°. The stated kite has opposite angles totaling 162°, so it cannot be cyclic.
geo33-foundation-p16.answerHtml: A cyclic quadrilateral must have opposite angles totaling 180°. The stated kite has opposite angles totaling 162°, so it cannot be cyclic.

methods.title: Check the opposite-angle condition
steps: A cyclic quadrilateral must have opposite angles totaling 180°. The stated kite has opposite angles totaling 162°, so it cannot be cyclic.

methods.title: Eliminate the three possible figures
steps: Every rectangle is cyclic because opposite right angles sum to 180°. Every isosceles trapezoid is cyclic for the same supplementary-opposite-angle reason. The vertices of every regular polygon lie on a circle. Only the stated kite fails.

geo33-foundation-p17.stem: AB is tangent at T to a circle with center O and radius 5 cm. The area of triangle AOB is 35 cm². What is AB (in cm)?
geo33-foundation-p17.stemRich: AB is tangent at T to a circle with center O and radius 5 cm. The area of triangle AOB is 35 cm². What is AB (in cm)?
geo33-foundation-p17.stemHtml: AB is tangent at T to a circle with center O and radius 5 cm. The area of triangle AOB is 35 cm². What is AB (in cm)?
explanation: OT is perpendicular to tangent AB, so it is a height of length 5. Thus 35=AB×5 divided by 2, giving AB=14.
geo33-foundation-p17.answerHtml: OT is perpendicular to tangent AB, so it is a height of length 5. Thus 35=AB×5 divided by 2, giving AB=14.

methods.title: Use the radius as the height
steps: OT is perpendicular to tangent AB, so it is a height of length 5. Thus 35=AB×5 divided by 2, giving AB=14.

methods.title: Use the doubled triangle area
steps: A rectangle with the same base and height would have twice the triangle area,70. Its height is 5, so its base is 70 divided by 5=14. This is the triangle-area formula read backwards.

geo33-foundation-p18.stemRich: AD and BC are diameters of two externally tangent circles. ABCD is a square with perimeter 28 cm. What is the sum of the circumferences of the circles (in cm)?
geo33-foundation-p18.stemHtml: AD and BC are diameters of two externally tangent circles. ABCD is a square with perimeter 28 cm. What is the sum of the circumferences of the circles (in cm)?
explanation: The square side is 28 divided by 4=7. Each circle diameter is 7, so each circumference is 7π and the sum is 14π.
geo33-foundation-p18.answerHtml: The square side is 28 divided by 4=7. Each circle diameter is 7, so each circumference is 7π and the sum is 14π.

methods.title: Use circumference equals pi times diameter
steps: The square side is 28 divided by 4=7. Each circle diameter is 7, so each circumference is 7π and the sum is 14π.

methods.title: Find both radii
steps: Each radius is 3.5. The sum of circumferences is 2π(3.5+3.5)=14π. There is no shared arc to subtract because the circles meet at only one point.

geo33-foundation-p19.stemHtml: A circle with center O has radius 8 cm. Three radii divide it into sectors of 135°, 90°, and a third angle. What is the length of the arc belonging to the third sector (in cm)?
explanation: The third angle is 360°−135°−90°=135°. Its arc takes 135:360=3:8 of circumference 16π, giving 6π.

methods.title: Find the remaining angle

methods.title: Subtract the other two arcs
steps: The 135° arc has length 6π and the 90° arc has length 4π. Subtract both from the full 16π circumference:16π−6π−4π=6π.

geo33-foundation-p20.stem: A circle with center O has area 25\pi cm². AB is a diameter and angle AOC is 36°. What is the area of sector COB contained in the same semicircle as C (in cm²)?
geo33-foundation-p20.stemRich: A circle with center O has area $25\pi$ cm². AB is a diameter and angle AOC is 36°. What is the area of sector COB contained in the same semicircle as C (in cm²)?
geo33-foundation-p20.stemHtml: A circle with center O has area cm². AB is a diameter and angle AOC is 36°. What is the area of sector COB contained in the same semicircle as C (in cm²)?
explanation: Angle COB=180°−36°=144°. The sector takes 144:360=2:5 of the disk, giving (2:5)×25π=10π.
geo33-foundation-p20.answerHtml: Angle COB=180°−36°=144°. The sector takes 144:360=2:5 of the disk, giving (2:5)×25π=10π.

methods.title: Find the sector fraction
steps: Angle COB=180°−36°=144°. The sector takes 144:360=2:5 of the disk, giving (2:5)×25π=10π.

methods.title: Subtract from a half disk
steps: The half disk area is 25π:2. The 36° sector is one tenth of the disk,5π:2. Their difference is 20π:2=10π.

geo33-foundation-p22.stem: A chord is 5 cm from the center of a circle with radius 13 cm. What is the length of the chord (in cm)?
geo33-foundation-p22.stemRich: A chord is 5 cm from the center of a circle with radius 13 cm. What is the length of the chord (in cm)?
geo33-foundation-p22.stemHtml: A chord is 5 cm from the center of a circle with radius 13 cm. What is the length of the chord (in cm)?
explanation: The perpendicular from the center bisects the chord. Half the chord has length √(13²−5²)=√144=12. Double it to get 24.
geo33-foundation-p22.answerHtml: The perpendicular from the center bisects the chord. Half the chord has length √(13²−5²)=√144=12. Double it to get 24.

methods.title: Use a right triangle on half the chord
steps: The perpendicular from the center bisects the chord. Half the chord has length √(13²−5²)=√144=12. Double it to get 24.

methods.title: Recognise a Pythagorean triple

geo33-g083.stemHtml: A circle with center O has radius 6 cm. Two non-overlapping shaded sectors have central angles of 60° and 90°. What is their total area (in cm²)?
explanation: The fractions are one sixth and one quarter, totaling five twelfths. The full area is 36π. Five twelfths of 36π is 15π.
geo33-g083.answerHtml: The fractions are one sixth and one quarter, totaling five twelfths. The full area is 36π. Five twelfths of 36π is 15π.

methods.title: Add the fractions before multiplying
steps: The fractions are one sixth and one quarter, totaling five twelfths. The full area is 36π. Five twelfths of 36π is 15π.

methods.title: Calculate each sector separately
steps: The 60° sector has area 36π divided by 6=6π. The 90° sector has area 36π divided by 4=9π. Their sum is 15π.

methods.title: Add the central angles
steps: The total shaded central measure is 150°. Thus the total area is 150 divided by 360 times 36π=15π.

geo33-g076.stemHtml: A, B and C lie on a circle with center O, with B on the minor arc AC. Given: angle AOC is 112°. What is angle ABC?
explanation: ABC intercepts the arc AC not containing B. Its central measure is 360°−112°=248°. The inscribed angle is half of 248°, or 124°.
geo33-g076.answerHtml: ABC intercepts the arc AC not containing B. Its central measure is 360°−112°=248°. The inscribed angle is half of 248°, or 124°.

methods.title: Use the major intercepted arc
steps: ABC intercepts the arc AC not containing B. Its central measure is 360°−112°=248°. The inscribed angle is half of 248°, or 124°.

methods.title: Add a point on the opposite arc
steps: Choose D on the major arc AC. Angle ADC intercepts the 112° minor arc, so it is 56°. ABCD is an inscribed quadrilateral, so the opposite angle ABC=180°−56°=124°.

methods.title: Use the two isosceles radius triangles
steps: Draw OB. Let angles ABO and OBC be u and v. Equal radii make the corresponding angles at A and C also u and v. The angle sums in AOB and BOC give central sum 360°−2(u+v). That sum is 112°, so u+v=124°.

geo37-g158.stem: A circle of radius 10 is centered at the origin O. A lies on the circle in the first quadrant and has y-coordinate 5. What is the angle between OA and the positive x-axis?
geo37-g158.stemRich: A circle of radius 10 is centered at the origin O. A lies on the circle in the first quadrant and has y-coordinate 5. What is the angle between OA and the positive x-axis?
geo37-g158.stemHtml: A circle of radius 10 is centered at the origin O. A lies on the circle in the first quadrant and has y-coordinate 5. What is the angle between OA and the positive x-axis?
explanation: Drop AH perpendicular to the x-axis. Then AH = 5 and OA = 10. A right-triangle leg equal to half the hypotenuse is opposite 30°, so angle AOH is 30°.
geo37-g158.answerHtml: Drop AH perpendicular to the x-axis. Then AH = 5 and OA = 10. A right-triangle leg equal to half the hypotenuse is opposite 30°, so angle AOH is 30°.

methods.title: Recognize a 30°–60°–90° triangle
steps: Drop AH perpendicular to the x-axis. Then AH = 5 and OA = 10. A right-triangle leg equal to half the hypotenuse is opposite 30°, so angle AOH is 30°.

methods.title: Reflect the point to make an equilateral triangle
steps: Reflect A across the x-axis to A′. Then AA′ = 10, and OA = OA′ = 10. Triangle OAA′ is equilateral, with central angle 60°. The x-axis bisects it by symmetry, so the requested angle is 30°.

geo37-g163.stem: A rectangle has sides parallel to the coordinate axes and opposite vertices (−2, 1) and (3, 9). It is rotated through a full turn about its right-hand vertical side. What is the volume of the solid formed?
geo37-g163.stemRich: A rectangle has sides parallel to the coordinate axes and opposite vertices (−2, 1) and (3, 9). It is rotated through a full turn about its right-hand vertical side. What is the volume of the solid formed?
geo37-g163.stemHtml: A rectangle has sides parallel to the coordinate axes and opposite vertices (−2, 1) and (3, 9). It is rotated through a full turn about its right-hand vertical side. What is the volume of the solid formed?
explanation: The width is 3−(−2) = 5 and the height is 9−1 = 8. Rotation about a vertical side forms a cylinder with radius 5 and height 8, so its volume is π×25×8 = 200π.
geo37-g163.answerHtml: The width is 3−(−2) = 5 and the height is 9−1 = 8. Rotation about a vertical side forms a cylinder with radius 5 and height 8, so its volume is π×25×8 = 200π.

methods.title: Read the cylinder radius and height from the rectangle
steps: The width is 3−(−2) = 5 and the height is 9−1 = 8. Rotation about a vertical side forms a cylinder with radius 5 and height 8, so its volume is π×25×8 = 200π.

methods.title: Follow one horizontal strip through the rotation
steps: Each horizontal segment from the rotation axis to the left side sweeps a disk of radius 5, area 25π. These equal cross sections extend through height 8, giving volume 200π.

geo37-g164.stemRich: A circle is centered at the origin O and passes through A(6, 6). B is its intersection with the negative y-axis. The two shaded regions together form the right semicircle with triangle OAB removed. What is their total area?
geo37-g164.stemHtml: A circle is centered at the origin O and passes through A(6, 6). B is its intersection with the negative y-axis. The two shaded regions together form the right semicircle with triangle OAB removed. What is their total area?
explanation: The radius squared is $6^2+6^2=72$, so the right semicircle area is $36\pi$. The base OB is $6\sqrt2$, and A’s perpendicular distance from the y-axis is 6. The triangle area is $\frac12(6\sqrt2)(6)=18\sqrt2$. Subtract to get $36\pi-18\sqrt2$.

methods.title: Subtract triangle area from semicircle area
steps: The radius squared is $6^2+6^2=72$, so the right semicircle area is $36\pi$. The base OB is $6\sqrt2$, and A’s perpendicular distance from the y-axis is 6. The triangle area is $\frac12(6\sqrt2)(6)=18\sqrt2$. Subtract to get $36\pi-18\sqrt2$.

methods.title: Use proved bounds to eliminate the other choices
steps: The semicircle area is $36\pi>108$. The triangle area is $3r$, and $r=6\sqrt2<9$, so the triangle area is below 27. Thus the shaded area exceeds 81. Using $\pi<\frac{22}{7}$ and $\sqrt2<\frac32$, the other choices are below 51, below 36, and negative, respectively. Only $36\pi-18\sqrt2$ can fit.

methods.title: Scale a unit-coordinate version
steps: For A(1,1), the radius is √2, the semicircle area is π, and the triangle area is √2 divided by 2. Scaling all lengths by 6 multiplies area by 36, giving $36(\pi-\frac{\sqrt2}{2})=36\pi-18\sqrt2$.

geo37-g165.stem: ABCDEF is a regular hexagon. Side CD lies on the positive x-axis, B lies on the positive y-axis, and C = (3, 0). The hexagon is shaded except for triangle AFE. What is the shaded area?
geo37-g165.stemRich: ABCDEF is a regular hexagon. Side CD lies on the positive x-axis, B lies on the positive y-axis, and C = (3, 0). The hexagon is shaded except for triangle AFE. What is the shaded area?
geo37-g165.stemHtml: ABCDEF is a regular hexagon. Side CD lies on the positive x-axis, B lies on the positive y-axis, and C = (3, 0). The hexagon is shaded except for triangle AFE. What is the shaded area?
explanation: The interior angle at C is 120°, so angle BCO is 60°. In right triangle BOC, OC = 3 is the short leg, making BC = 6. A regular hexagon contains six equilateral triangles of side 6, each with area 9√3. Corner triangle AFE has the same area as one of those triangles. The shaded area is 5×9√3 = 45√3.
geo37-g165.answerHtml: The interior angle at C is 120°, so angle BCO is 60°. In right triangle BOC, OC = 3 is the short leg, making BC = 6. A regular hexagon contains six equilateral triangles of side 6, each with area 9√3. Corner triangle AFE has the same area as one of those triangles. The shaded area is 5×9√3 = 45√3.

methods.title: Find the side, then subtract one sixth of the area
steps: The interior angle at C is 120°, so angle BCO is 60°. In right triangle BOC, OC = 3 is the short leg, making BC = 6. A regular hexagon contains six equilateral triangles of side 6, each with area 9√3. Corner triangle AFE has the same area as one of those triangles. The shaded area is 5×9√3 = 45√3.

methods.title: Calculate the whole and corner areas directly
steps: The hexagon area is $\frac{3\sqrt3}{2}\times6^2=54\sqrt3$. Triangle AFE has equal sides 6 with included angle 120°; dropping its altitude gives base $6\sqrt3$ and height 3, so its area is $9\sqrt3$. The difference is $45\sqrt3$.

geo37-g166.stemRich: Line n passes through the origin and C(10, 4). Line m is parallel to n and passes through A(5, 7) and B(0, b). What are the coordinates of B?
geo37-g166.stemHtml: Line n passes through the origin and C(10, 4). Line m is parallel to n and passes through A(5, 7) and B(0, b). What are the coordinates of B?
explanation: Line n has slope $\frac4{10}=\frac25$. Moving 5 units left from A to the y-axis lowers the line by 2 units. Thus b = 7 − 2 = 5.
geo37-g166.answerHtml: Line n has slope . Moving 5 units left from A to the y-axis lowers the line by 2 units. Thus b = 7 − 2 = 5.

methods.title: Use equal slopes
steps: Line n has slope $\frac4{10}=\frac25$. Moving 5 units left from A to the y-axis lowers the line by 2 units. Thus b = 7 − 2 = 5.

methods.title: Use a line equation
steps: Write line m as $y=\frac25x+b$. Substitute A(5,7): $7=2+b$, so b = 5.

methods.title: Compare the two right triangles
steps: The origin-to-C triangle has horizontal leg 10 and vertical leg 4. The B-to-A triangle has horizontal leg 5, half as large, so its vertical rise is 2. B is therefore 2 below A, at y = 5.

geo37-core-p02.stemHtml: A(6, 0), B(0, −2) and C lie on one straight line, with B between A and C. Given: AB = BC. What are the coordinates of C?
explanation: From A to B, move 6 left and 2 down. Equal consecutive segments on the same line repeat that move, giving C(−6,−4).
geo37-core-p02.answerHtml: From A to B, move 6 left and 2 down. Equal consecutive segments on the same line repeat that move, giving C(−6,−4).

methods.title: Repeat the same coordinate change
steps: From A to B, move 6 left and 2 down. Equal consecutive segments on the same line repeat that move, giving C(−6,−4).

methods.title: Use the midpoint formula
steps: B is the midpoint of AC. Thus $\frac{6+x_C}{2}=0$ and $\frac{0+y_C}{2}=-2$, giving x_C = −6 and y_C = −4.

methods.title: Use congruent projection triangles
steps: Drop perpendiculars to the axes. The right triangles representing AB and BC have equal hypotenuses and the same acute angle, so their horizontal and vertical legs are equal. Each step is 6 horizontally and 2 vertically.

geo37-core-p11.stemHtml: ABCDEF is a regular hexagon. AB lies on the positive x-axis, F lies on the positive y-axis, and B = (6, 0). What is the radius of the circle circumscribing the hexagon?

explanation: AD is horizontal, so D has y-coordinate t. Let E be its projection onto the x-axis. Triangle CED has angle C = 60°, vertical leg DE = t, and horizontal leg CE = t divided by √3. Thus x_D = 2t+t divided by √3.

methods.title: Use the 30°–60°–90° leg ratio
steps: The line CD makes a 60° angle with the horizontal. Its vertical change t is √3 times its positive horizontal change. Therefore the horizontal change from C to D is t divided by √3, which we add to 2t.

geo37-core-p20.stemHtml: A(n, 6), B(−1, −2) and C(1, 0) lie on one straight line. What is n?
explanation: From B to C, move 2 right and 2 up. The line rises one unit for each unit right. To rise 6 from C to A, move 6 right, giving n = 1+6 = 7.
geo37-core-p20.answerHtml: From B to C, move 2 right and 2 up. The line rises one unit for each unit right. To rise 6 from C to A, move 6 right, giving n = 1+6 = 7.

methods.title: Repeat the equal horizontal and vertical changes
steps: From B to C, move 2 right and 2 up. The line rises one unit for each unit right. To rise 6 from C to A, move 6 right, giving n = 1+6 = 7.

methods.title: Use similar right triangles
steps: The right triangle under BC has equal legs. The corresponding triangle between C and A is also right isosceles, so its horizontal leg n−1 equals its vertical leg 6. Hence n = 7.

methods.title: Write the line equation
steps: The slope is 1 and the x-intercept is 1, so y = x−1. Substituting A gives 6 = n−1, hence n = 7.

geo37-core-p27.stem: Line a passes through (−2, −1) and (4, 3). Line b is parallel to a and passes through (3, 8). At what point does b intersect the y-axis?
geo37-core-p27.stemRich: Line a passes through (−2, −1) and (4, 3). Line b is parallel to a and passes through (3, 8). At what point does b intersect the y-axis?
geo37-core-p27.stemHtml: Line a passes through (−2, −1) and (4, 3). Line b is parallel to a and passes through (3, 8). At what point does b intersect the y-axis?
explanation: On a, moving 6 right raises y by 4, so moving 3 left lowers y by 2. Apply that move from (3,8) on parallel line b: the y-axis point is (0,6).
geo37-core-p27.answerHtml: On a, moving 6 right raises y by 4, so moving 3 left lowers y by 2. Apply that move from (3,8) on parallel line b: the y-axis point is (0,6).

methods.title: Use the same rise for the same horizontal move
steps: On a, moving 6 right raises y by 4, so moving 3 left lowers y by 2. Apply that move from (3,8) on parallel line b: the y-axis point is (0,6).

methods.title: Use the slope-intercept equation
steps: The slope is $\frac{3-(-1)}{4-(-2)}=\frac23$. Write b as $y=\frac23x+c$. Substituting (3,8) gives 8 = 2+c, so c = 6.

geo37-g160.stemHtml: A line passes through the origin and A(−2a, −2b), with a and b being positive and a ≠ b. Which of the following cannot be the coordinates of a point B on this line in the first quadrant?
explanation: The line has x-to-y ratio a : b. The cubic pair would require $\frac{a^3}{b^3}=\frac ab$, giving a² = b². Positivity then gives a = b, contrary to the condition. The other pairs all simplify to a : b.
geo37-g160.answerHtml: The line has x-to-y ratio a : b. The cubic pair would require , giving a² = b². Positivity then gives a = b, contrary to the condition. The other pairs all simplify to a : b.

methods.title: Compare the coordinate ratios
steps: The line has x-to-y ratio a : b. The cubic pair would require $\frac{a^3}{b^3}=\frac ab$, giving a² = b². Positivity then gives a = b, contrary to the condition. The other pairs all simplify to a : b.

methods.title: Check for a common multiplier
steps: Every point on the origin line is a scalar multiple of (a, b). The pair (a³, b³) would need both multiplier a² and multiplier b²; these differ because a and b are positive and unequal. The other pairs use multipliers 3, $\frac1{ab}$, and $\frac12$.

methods.title: Use the line equation
steps: The slope is $\frac ba$, so the equation is $ay=bx$. Substituting (a³, b³) yields ab³ = ba³, equivalent to b² = a², impossible under the given conditions.

geo34-g114.stemHtml: The accompanying figure shows a regular octagon. AB and CD are perpendicular and intersect at E. A, B, C and D are vertices of the octagon, as shown in the figure. Lina claims that . Noam claims that the perimeter of triangle ACE equals CD. Which of the following is true?
explanation: Let AE=CE=3. The octagon side AC is 3√2. BE=3+3√2>6=2 AE, so Lina is correct. The triangle perimeter is 6+3√2. Segment CD consists of two corner offsets of 3 and a middle length 3√2, also 6+3√2. Noam is correct too.
geo34-g114.answerHtml: Let AE=CE=3. The octagon side AC is 3√2. BE=3+3√2>6=2 AE, so Lina is correct. The triangle perimeter is 6+3√2. Segment CD consists of two corner offsets of 3 and a middle length 3√2, also 6+3√2. Noam is correct too.

methods.title: Choose a convenient corner-triangle leg
steps: Let AE=CE=3. The octagon side AC is 3√2. BE=3+3√2>6=2 AE, so Lina is correct. The triangle perimeter is 6+3√2. Segment CD consists of two corner offsets of 3 and a middle length 3√2, also 6+3√2. Noam is correct too.

methods.title: Match segments without calculating a radical
steps: Write the corner leg as t and the octagon side as s. Because s is the hypotenuse of a right isosceles triangle, s>t. Thus BE=s+t>2t=2 AE. Also CD=t+s+t, exactly the sum of triangle ACE’s sides t, s, t. Both claims hold.

geo34-g115.stemHtml: The accompanying figure shows a regular octagon divided by two vertical segments. The central white rectangle has area cm². What is the sum of the shaded areas (in cm²)?
explanation: The white rectangle contains the central square and two of the four congruent rectangles. The shaded parts contain the other two rectangles and four corner triangles. The four triangles together equal the central square in area, so shaded and white totals are equal.
geo34-g115.answerHtml: The white rectangle contains the central square and two of the four congruent rectangles. The shaded parts contain the other two rectangles and four corner triangles. The four triangles together equal the central square in area, so shaded and white totals are equal.

methods.title: Match the areas in the standard partition
steps: The white rectangle contains the central square and two of the four congruent rectangles. The shaded parts contain the other two rectangles and four corner triangles. The four triangles together equal the central square in area, so shaded and white totals are equal.

methods.title: Use the regular-octagon formula
steps: For side s, the white rectangle has width s and height s+s√2, so its area is s²(1+√2). The whole octagon area is 2s²(1+√2), twice the white area. The shaded remainder equals the white area.

methods.title: Compare the left and right halves with the middle
steps: Each shaded side consists of one rectangle and two corner triangles. The two triangles together have half the central square’s area. Two shaded sides therefore match two rectangles plus one square, exactly the white region.

methods.title: Count 180-degree steps from an octagon

methods.title: Count the triangles in a triangulation
steps: The angle sum contains 1620:180=9 triangle totals. A polygon with n sides triangulates into n−2 triangles. Thus n−2=9 and n=11.

geo34-g117.stemHtml: A is the sum of the interior angles of a 12-sided polygon, and B is the sum of the interior angles of a 17-sided polygon. The difference equals the sum of the interior angles of which polygon?

geo34-g117.answerHtml: B−A=180(17−2)−180(12−2)=180(15−10)=900°. A polygon with angle sum 900° has n−2=5, so n=7: a heptagon.

methods.title: Count the extra sides first

explanation: Triangle AED has perpendicular legs 12 and 5, so its area is 30 and AD=13. Drop AH perpendicular to CD. ABCH is a square of side 12. Triangle ADH has hypotenuse 13 and height 12, so DH=5 and its area is 30. The total is 144+30+30=204.

methods.title: Split into a square and two right triangles
steps: Triangle AED has perpendicular legs 12 and 5, so its area is 30 and AD=13. Drop AH perpendicular to CD. ABCH is a square of side 12. Triangle ADH has hypotenuse 13 and height 12, so DH=5 and its area is 30. The total is 144+30+30=204.

methods.title: Add one triangle to a trapezoid
steps: AD=13 from the 5–12–13 triangle AED. Dropping AH gives DH=5, so CD=17. Trapezoid ABCD has parallel bases 12 and 17 and height 12, giving area 174. Add triangle AED of area 30 to get 204.

geo34-g108.stemHtml: A regular octagon has side length 5 cm. What is its area (in cm²)?
explanation: The central square has area 25. Each corner right isosceles triangle has hypotenuse 5, so its legs are 5:√2 and its area 25:4. The four triangles total 25. Each rectangle has sides 5 and 5:√2 and area 25√2:2; four total 50√2. Altogether the area is 50+50√2.
geo34-g108.answerHtml: The central square has area 25. Each corner right isosceles triangle has hypotenuse 5, so its legs are 5:√2 and its area 25:4. The four triangles total 25. Each rectangle has sides 5 and 5:√2 and area 25√2:2; four total 50√2. Altogether the area is 50+50√2.

methods.title: Add the central square, four triangles and four rectangles
steps: The central square has area 25. Each corner right isosceles triangle has hypotenuse 5, so its legs are 5:√2 and its area 25:4. The four triangles total 25. Each rectangle has sides 5 and 5:√2 and area 25√2:2; four total 50√2. Altogether the area is 50+50√2.

methods.title: Subtract four corners from a surrounding square
steps: The bounding square side is 5+5√2. Its area is 75+50√2. The four removed corner right triangles each have area 25:4, totaling 25. The difference is 50+50√2.

methods.title: Use the derived regular-octagon formula
steps: For side s, the same partition gives area 2s²(1+√2). Substituting s=5 gives 50(1+√2)=50+50√2.

geo34-g110.stemRich: ABCDE is a regular pentagon. What is angle ADB?
geo34-g110.stemHtml: ABCDE is a regular pentagon. What is angle ADB?
explanation: Each pentagon interior angle is 108°. Triangles BCD and DEA have equal adjacent polygon sides and vertex angle 108°, so their base angles at D are 36° each. The requested angle is 108°−36°−36°=36°.
geo34-g110.answerHtml: Each pentagon interior angle is 108°. Triangles BCD and DEA have equal adjacent polygon sides and vertex angle 108°, so their base angles at D are 36° each. The requested angle is 108°−36°−36°=36°.

methods.title: Subtract two isosceles-triangle angles
steps: Each pentagon interior angle is 108°. Triangles BCD and DEA have equal adjacent polygon sides and vertex angle 108°, so their base angles at D are 36° each. The requested angle is 108°−36°−36°=36°.

methods.title: Use the circumscribed circle
steps: Adjacent vertices A and B cut off one fifth of the circle, an arc of 72°. Inscribed angle ADB is half that arc measure, or 36°.

methods.title: Use the trapezoid left by a diagonal
steps: Diagonal DB leaves isosceles trapezoid EABD, whose base angle EDB is 72°. In triangle EAD, equal sides EA and ED give angle EDA=36°. Subtracting leaves angle ADB=36°.

methods.title: Use equal angle pieces from one vertex
steps: The two diagonals from D divide its 108° interior angle into three equal pieces, because they intercept equal side-arcs. Each piece, including ADB, is 36°.

geo34-g111.stemHtml: A regular octagon ABCDEFGH is inscribed in a circle with center O and radius r. Which of the following statements is not true?
choices: The perimeter of the octagon is 8r.
The circumference of the circle is greater than the perimeter of the octagon.
choicesRich: The perimeter of the octagon is $8r$.
The circumference of the circle is greater than the perimeter of the octagon.
choicesHtml: The perimeter of the octagon is .
The circumference of the circle is greater than the perimeter of the octagon.
explanation: Each central triangle has vertex angle 45° and base angles 67.5°. The octagon side faces 45°, while each radius faces 67.5°. Thus each side is shorter than r and the perimeter is less than 8r, so equality is false.
geo34-g111.answerHtml: Each central triangle has vertex angle 45° and base angles 67.5°. The octagon side faces 45°, while each radius faces 67.5°. Thus each side is shorter than r and the perimeter is less than 8r, so equality is false.

methods.title: Compare a polygon side with a radius
steps: Each central triangle has vertex angle 45° and base angles 67.5°. The octagon side faces 45°, while each radius faces 67.5°. Thus each side is shorter than r and the perimeter is less than 8r, so equality is false.

methods.title: Eliminate the three true statements
steps: The central angles between adjacent radii are all 45°. Each circle arc is longer than its chord, so the circumference exceeds the polygon perimeter. The two central triangles on either side of OC are congruent, so BCO=OCD. Only the 8r statement is false.

methods.title: Use a circumference upper bound
steps: An inscribed polygon’s perimeter is less than the circumference 2πr. Since π<4, the circumference is less than 8r. Therefore the octagon perimeter cannot equal 8r.

geo34-g112.stem: ABCDEF is a regular hexagon. The perimeter of triangle ACE is 30 cm. What is the perimeter of the hexagon (in cm)?
geo34-g112.stemRich: ABCDEF is a regular hexagon. The perimeter of triangle ACE is 30 cm. What is the perimeter of the hexagon (in cm)?
geo34-g112.stemHtml: ABCDEF is a regular hexagon. The perimeter of triangle ACE is 30 cm. What is the perimeter of the hexagon (in cm)?
explanation: Triangle ACE is equilateral, so AC=10. Triangle ABC is isosceles with vertex angle 120°. Its altitude from B bisects AC into 5 and 5 and forms a special right triangle. The hexagon side is 10:√3. Six sides give 60:√3=20√3.
geo34-g112.answerHtml: Triangle ACE is equilateral, so AC=10. Triangle ABC is isosceles with vertex angle 120°. Its altitude from B bisects AC into 5 and 5 and forms a special right triangle. The hexagon side is 10:√3. Six sides give 60:√3=20√3.

methods.title: Use a30°–60°–90° triangle
steps: Triangle ACE is equilateral, so AC=10. Triangle ABC is isosceles with vertex angle 120°. Its altitude from B bisects AC into 5 and 5 and forms a special right triangle. The hexagon side is 10:√3. Six sides give 60:√3=20√3.

methods.title: Use a strict perimeter bound to eliminate choices
steps: Each side of ACE is shorter than the two hexagon sides joining its endpoints, so the hexagon perimeter exceeds 30. Since √3<7:4, 17√3<29.75. Since √2<3:2, both 17√2 and 20√2 are less than 30. Only 20√3 remains.

methods.title: Use the chord length in the central triangles
steps: The short diagonal AC spans a120° central angle. Splitting its central isosceles triangle in half gives AC=√3 times the hexagon side. Therefore the hexagon perimeter is 6×10:√3=20√3.

explanation: The three corner triangles together make half the hexagon. The whole area is 6×(6²√3:4)=54√3. Half is 27√3.

methods.title: Use the half-hexagon partition

methods.title: Calculate one corner triangle directly
steps: Its equal sides are 6 and its vertex angle 120°. The altitude splits it into two 30°–60°–90° triangles, giving base 6√3 and height 3. Its area is 9√3; three such triangles total 27√3.

geo34-g113.stemRich: Four squares are constructed externally on four sides of a regular hexagon. Maya claims that the sum of the four square perimeters is 3 times the hexagon perimeter. Daniel claims that the sum of the four square areas is greater than the hexagon area. Which of the following is true?
geo34-g113.stemHtml: Four squares are constructed externally on four sides of a regular hexagon. Maya claims that the sum of the four square perimeters is 3 times the hexagon perimeter. Daniel claims that the sum of the four square areas is greater than the hexagon area. Which of the following is true?
explanation: Choose common side 3. The four square perimeters total 48, while the hexagon perimeter is 18;48 is not three times 18. The square areas total 36. The hexagon area is 27√3:2, which is less than 27 and hence less than 36. Only Daniel is correct.
geo34-g113.answerHtml: Choose common side 3. The four square perimeters total 48, while the hexagon perimeter is 18;48 is not three times 18. The square areas total 36. The hexagon area is 27√3:2, which is less than 27 and hence less than 36. Only Daniel is correct.

methods.title: Use a convenient side length
steps: Choose common side 3. The four square perimeters total 48, while the hexagon perimeter is 18;48 is not three times 18. The square areas total 36. The hexagon area is 27√3:2, which is less than 27 and hence less than 36. Only Daniel is correct.

methods.title: Count equal sides and compare with rhombi
steps: The squares have 16 side-length units of perimeter; the hexagon has 6, so their ratio is 8:3, not 3. Divide the hexagon into three 60° rhombi, each of the same side length as a square. Each rhombus has smaller height and area than a square. Three squares already exceed the hexagon area, so four do too.

geo34-core-p01.stemRich: ABCDEF is a regular hexagon with side length 3 cm. AB and FE are extended to meet line CD at G and H, respectively. What is the perimeter of trapezoid AGHF (in cm)?
geo34-core-p01.stemHtml: ABCDEF is a regular hexagon with side length 3 cm. AB and FE are extended to meet line CD at G and H, respectively. What is the perimeter of trapezoid AGHF (in cm)?
explanation: Each external base angle beside the hexagon is 60°, so triangles GBC and HED are equilateral with side 3. Thus AG=FH=6, GH=9 and AF=3. Their sum is 24.
geo34-core-p01.answerHtml: Each external base angle beside the hexagon is 60°, so triangles GBC and HED are equilateral with side 3. Thus AG=FH=6, GH=9 and AF=3. Their sum is 24.

methods.title: Find the two added equilateral triangles
steps: Each external base angle beside the hexagon is 60°, so triangles GBC and HED are equilateral with side 3. Thus AG=FH=6, GH=9 and AF=3. Their sum is 24.

methods.title: Count equal side-length units
steps: The top base contains one side unit, the bottom three, and each sloping side two. There are 1+3+2+2=8 units, each 3 cm, so the perimeter is 24. The equal units follow from the 60° exterior angles.

methods.title: Count five radius lengths
steps: A regular hexagon’s circumradius equals its side. The horizontal segment crosses five such radius-length units in this arrangement. Five times 2.4 is 12. The central pair’s shared horizontal side has the same length.

explanation: Each octagon contributes five sides to the outside boundary, giving 20 equal sides. The sum of the four full perimeters contains 32 sides. The ratio 20:32 reduces to 5:8.

methods.title: Remove the internal boundaries from the full perimeter sum
steps: The four octagon-to-octagon shared sides are each counted twice, so remove 8 side units. The four sides facing the central hole are also excluded, leaving 32−8−4=20. Divide by 32 to get 5:8.

geo34-core-p08.stemHtml: Two congruent regular heptagons share one entire side and lie on opposite sides of it. The perimeter of their combined outer boundary is 84 cm. What is the perimeter of one heptagon (in cm)?
explanation: The shared side is absent from the outer boundary. There are 14−2=12 exposed equal sides. Each is 84:12=7 cm, so one seven-sided perimeter is 49 cm.
geo34-core-p08.answerHtml: The shared side is absent from the outer boundary. There are 14−2=12 exposed equal sides. Each is 84:12=7 cm, so one seven-sided perimeter is 49 cm.

methods.title: Count the outer sides
steps: The shared side is absent from the outer boundary. There are 14−2=12 exposed equal sides. Each is 84:12=7 cm, so one seven-sided perimeter is 49 cm.

methods.title: Relate the two perimeters algebraically
steps: If a side is s, the outer boundary is 2×7s−2s=12s=84. Thus s=7 and the single-heptagon perimeter is 7s=49.

geo34-core-p10.stemHtml: Eight congruent circles of radius 2 cm have centers at the vertices of a regular octagon. Each circle is externally tangent to its two neighbors. What is the sum of the areas of the parts of the disks lying outside the octagon (in cm²)?
explanation: At each octagon vertex, the disk portion inside the polygon is a135° sector. The outside part is 225°, or 5:8 of the disk. Eight such portions total five full disks, giving 5×4π=20π.
geo34-core-p10.answerHtml: At each octagon vertex, the disk portion inside the polygon is a135° sector. The outside part is 225°, or 5:8 of the disk. Eight such portions total five full disks, giving 5×4π=20π.

methods.title: Calculate one outside sector and multiply
steps: At each octagon vertex, the disk portion inside the polygon is a135° sector. The outside part is 225°, or 5:8 of the disk. Eight such portions total five full disks, giving 5×4π=20π.

methods.title: Subtract all inside sectors from the disk total
steps: The eight disks total 32π. Their inside sector angles total 8×135°=1080°, equivalent to three full disks of radius 2, area 12π. Subtract to obtain 20π.

explanation: A parallelogram has exactly two diagonals, and they intersect at their common midpoint inside it. Thus all its diagonals meet at one interior point.

methods.title: Use the two diagonals of a quadrilateral

methods.title: Eliminate polygons with at least five vertices
steps: In any convex polygon with at least five vertices, one vertex has at least two distinct diagonals. Those two segments meet only at that vertex and cannot share an interior intersection. Therefore all diagonals of such a polygon cannot pass through one interior point.

steps: Let AE=x, ED=y and the common height be h. The given areas are xh divided by 2=5 and yh divided by 2=13. The shaded area is (x+y)h divided by 2, which equals 5+13=18.

methods.title: Use half of the whole rectangle
steps: EBC has the rectangle’s full base and height, so it has half the rectangle’s area. The two white triangles cover the other half and total 18. The shaded half is therefore 18 as well.

methods.title: Compare fixed fractions of the rectangle
steps: EG splits the rectangle into widths in the ratio 2:1. Triangle ECD is half the right third, or one sixth of the whole. The shaded FEG is half the left two thirds and EGC is half the right third, totaling one half. Therefore the shaded area is three times ECD.

methods.title: Use area variables and check the missing freedom
steps: Let ED=w and height=h. ECD has area wh divided by 2; the shaded area is 3 wh divided by 2. Either AFE or FBG fixes a product involving only part of h, whose division at F is unknown. Thus those areas alone cannot fix the total.

geo32-g069.stem: ABCD is an isosceles trapezoid with AD\parallel BC, AD=4 cm and BC=12 cm. The shaded triangle ABD has area 14 cm². What is the area of the trapezoid (in cm²)?
geo32-g069.stemRich: ABCD is an isosceles trapezoid with $AD\parallel BC$, $AD=4$ cm and $BC=12$ cm. The shaded triangle ABD has area 14 cm². What is the area of the trapezoid (in cm²)?
geo32-g069.stemHtml: ABCD is an isosceles trapezoid with , cm and cm. The shaded triangle ABD has area 14 cm². What is the area of the trapezoid (in cm²)?
explanation: Triangles ABD and BCD have bases 4 and 12 on the parallel lines, and the same perpendicular height. Their areas are in the ratio 1:3. Thus BCD has area 42, and the whole trapezoid has area 14+42=56.
geo32-g069.answerHtml: Triangles ABD and BCD have bases 4 and 12 on the parallel lines, and the same perpendicular height. Their areas are in the ratio 1:3. Thus BCD has area 42, and the whole trapezoid has area 14+42=56.

methods.title: Use the shared height
steps: Triangles ABD and BCD have bases 4 and 12 on the parallel lines, and the same perpendicular height. Their areas are in the ratio 1:3. Thus BCD has area 42, and the whole trapezoid has area 14+42=56.

methods.title: Find the height and use the trapezoid formula
steps: The shaded triangle gives 4h divided by 2=14, so h=7. The trapezoid area is (4+12)×7 divided by 2=56.

methods.title: Split the larger-base triangle into three equal areas
steps: Divide BC into three 4 cm pieces and join their endpoints to D. Each resulting triangle has the same base length and height as ABD, so each has area 14. Four such areas cover the trapezoid, giving 56.

geo32-g070.stemHtml: The rectangle in the accompanying figure consists of 35 congruent squares, each with side length 1 cm. What is the shaded area (in cm²)?
explanation: The whole rectangle has area 35. The unshaded corner triangles have perpendicular legs 1 and 2,6 and 2,2 and 3, and 2 and 3. Their areas are 1,6,3,3, totaling 13. The shaded area is 35−13=22.
geo32-g070.answerHtml: The whole rectangle has area 35. The unshaded corner triangles have perpendicular legs 1 and 2,6 and 2,2 and 3, and 2 and 3. Their areas are 1,6,3,3, totaling 13. The shaded area is 35−13=22.

methods.title: Subtract four corner triangles
steps: The whole rectangle has area 35. The unshaded corner triangles have perpendicular legs 1 and 2,6 and 2,2 and 3, and 2 and 3. Their areas are 1,6,3,3, totaling 13. The shaded area is 35−13=22.

methods.title: Add familiar pieces inside the shading
steps: Split horizontally at the two side vertices. The upper shaded triangle has base 7 and height 2, area 7. The lower shaded trapezoid has bases 7 and 3 and height 3, area 15. Their sum is 22.

methods.title: Split the lower region into a rectangle and two triangles
steps: The upper shaded triangle contributes 7. Below it, the middle 3 by 3 rectangle contributes 9, and the two side right triangles each contribute 3. The total is 7+9+3+3=22.

explanation: Angle D=250°−α−β. Its half at ADE is 125°−α divided by 2−β divided by 2. Therefore angle AED=180°−α−angle ADE=55°−α divided by 2+β divided by 2.

methods.title: Use the quadrilateral and triangle angle sums
steps: Angle D=250°−α−β. Its half at ADE is 125°−α divided by 2−β divided by 2. Therefore angle AED=180°−α−angle ADE=55°−α divided by 2+β divided by 2.

methods.title: Substitute a valid unequal pair
steps: Take α=108° and β=82°. Angle D is 60°, its half is 30°, and angle AED=42°. The expression 55°−α divided by 2+β divided by 2 gives 42°. The alternatives give 68°,97° and 123°, so all three are eliminated. The full algebra proves the rule for all allowed values.

geo32-g072.stem: Rectangle ABCD consists of six congruent rectangles, arranged as in the accompanying figure. The perimeter of ABCD is 50 cm. What is its area (in cm²)?
geo32-g072.stemRich: Rectangle ABCD consists of six congruent rectangles, arranged as in the accompanying figure. The perimeter of ABCD is 50 cm. What is its area (in cm²)?
geo32-g072.stemHtml: Rectangle ABCD consists of six congruent rectangles, arranged as in the accompanying figure. The perimeter of ABCD is 50 cm. What is its area (in cm²)?
explanation: Let the short side of a small rectangle be x. Four horizontal copies stack to the height of a vertical one, so the long side is 4x. The large rectangle measures 6x by 4x. Its perimeter 20x=50 gives x=2.5. Its area is 24x²=150.
geo32-g072.answerHtml: Let the short side of a small rectangle be x. Four horizontal copies stack to the height of a vertical one, so the long side is 4x. The large rectangle measures 6x by 4x. Its perimeter 20x=50 gives x=2.5. Its area is 24x²=150.

methods.title: Read the small-rectangle ratio from the arrangement
steps: Let the short side of a small rectangle be x. Four horizontal copies stack to the height of a vertical one, so the long side is 4x. The large rectangle measures 6x by 4x. Its perimeter 20x=50 gives x=2.5. Its area is 24x²=150.

methods.title: Use the large rectangle’s side ratio
steps: The arrangement gives large side ratio 6:4=3:2. Since the semiperimeter is 25, five ratio units total 25 and each is 5. The large sides are 15 and 10, so its area is 150.

geo32-g057.stem: The accompanying figure shows quadrilateral ABCD. Given: angle A is 112° and angle B is 104°. Which of the following cannot be the value of α?

geo32-g057.stemHtml: The accompanying figure shows quadrilateral ABCD. Given: angle A is 112° and angle B is 104°. Which of the following cannot be the value of α?
explanation: They sum to 360°−112°−104°=144°. Each is positive, so α must be strictly less than 144°. The choice 144° would force the other angle to 0°.
geo32-g057.answerHtml: They sum to 360°−112°−104°=144°. Each is positive, so α must be strictly less than 144°. The choice 144° would force the other angle to 0°.

methods.title: Find the sum of the two remaining angles

methods.title: Test the implied fourth angle

geo32-g059.stemRich: The diagonals of rectangle ABCD intersect at E. Given: $BC=12$ cm, and the perimeter of triangle EBC is 25 cm. What is the area of triangle ABE (in cm²)?
geo32-g059.stemHtml: The diagonals of rectangle ABCD intersect at E. Given: cm, and the perimeter of triangle EBC is 25 cm. What is the area of triangle ABE (in cm²)?
explanation: EB=EC and their sum is 25−12=13, so each half-diagonal is 6.5 and AC=13. The rectangle’s other side is √(13²−12²)=5. The diagonals divide its area 60 into four equal areas, so ABE has area 15.
geo32-g059.answerHtml: EB=EC and their sum is 25−12=13, so each half-diagonal is 6.5 and AC=13. The rectangle’s other side is √(13²−12²)=5. The diagonals divide its area 60 into four equal areas, so ABE has area 15.

methods.title: Find the rectangle, then take one quarter
steps: EB=EC and their sum is 25−12=13, so each half-diagonal is 6.5 and AC=13. The rectangle’s other side is √(13²−12²)=5. The diagonals divide its area 60 into four equal areas, so ABE has area 15.

methods.title: Use the median in triangle ABC
steps: After finding AB=5, the area of ABC is 5×12 divided by 2=30. Since E is the midpoint of AC, BE is a median. It divides ABC into equal-area triangles ABE and EBC, so ABE has area 15.

methods.title: Use a direct perpendicular height
steps: The base AB is 5, and E is halfway across the rectangle, so its perpendicular distance from AB is 6. The requested area is 5×6 divided by 2=15.

geo32-g060.stemHtml: ABCD is a rhombus. Given: cm and angle ABD is 60°. What is the area of the rhombus (in cm²)?
explanation: AB=AD, so triangle ABD is isosceles. Its 60° base angle makes it equilateral, with side 6. All rhombus sides are 6, so BCD is equilateral too. Twice 6²√3 divided by 4 gives 18√3.
geo32-g060.answerHtml: AB=AD, so triangle ABD is isosceles. Its 60° base angle makes it equilateral, with side 6. All rhombus sides are 6, so BCD is equilateral too. Twice 6²√3 divided by 4 gives 18√3.

methods.title: Use two equilateral triangles
steps: AB=AD, so triangle ABD is isosceles. Its 60° base angle makes it equilateral, with side 6. All rhombus sides are 6, so BCD is equilateral too. Twice 6²√3 divided by 4 gives 18√3.

methods.title: Find the other diagonal using a special triangle
steps: Draw AC meeting BD at O. Then BO=3 and angle ABO=60°. The right triangle ABO has AO=3√3. Thus AC=6√3, and the area is 6×6√3 divided by 2=18√3.

methods.title: Add four small right triangles
steps: Each small triangle between the diagonals has legs 3 and 3√3. Its area is 9√3 divided by 2. Four copies cover 18√3.

methods.title: Find the isosceles triangle ABO

methods.title: Use the equal-side chain and the angle sum directly
steps: Let the requested angle be x. Then angle ABO=90°−x. Since AB=AO, angle AOB is also 90°−x. The sum 30°+2(90°−x)=180° gives x=15°.

methods.title: Complete the diagonals

methods.title: Add the four right-triangle areas

geo32-advanced-p03.stemHtml: ABCD is an isosceles trapezoid with . Given: cm, cm and angle BAC is 90°. What is α?
explanation: In right triangle ABC, BC=18 is twice AB=9. Thus angle ACB is 30° and angle ABC is 60°. The opposite upper angle in an isosceles trapezoid is supplementary to B, so α=120°.
geo32-advanced-p03.answerHtml: In right triangle ABC, BC=18 is twice AB=9. Thus angle ACB is 30° and angle ABC is 60°. The opposite upper angle in an isosceles trapezoid is supplementary to B, so α=120°.

methods.title: Recognise the half-hypotenuse relationship
steps: In right triangle ABC, BC=18 is twice AB=9. Thus angle ACB is 30° and angle ABC is 60°. The opposite upper angle in an isosceles trapezoid is supplementary to B, so α=120°.

methods.title: Find the two parts of the upper-left angle
steps: The right triangle gives angle ACB=30°. Parallel bases make angle CAD=30°. Adding angle BAC=90° gives angle BAD=120°. The upper base angles of an isosceles trapezoid are equal, so α=120°.
