geo32-advanced-p04.stemRich: ABCD is a square with side length 8 cm. Triangle AED is equilateral and lies inside the square. F lies on AB, with $EF\parallel AD$. What is the area of the shaded triangle AFE (in cm²)?
geo32-advanced-p04.stemHtml: ABCD is a square with side length 8 cm. Triangle AED is equilateral and lies inside the square. F lies on AB, with . What is the area of the shaded triangle AFE (in cm²)?
explanation: The altitude of the equilateral triangle is 4√3. Thus AF=4√3. Symmetry places E halfway across the 8 cm base, so FE=4. The shaded right triangle has area 4×4√3 divided by 2=8√3.
geo32-advanced-p04.answerHtml: The altitude of the equilateral triangle is 4√3. Thus AF=4√3. Symmetry places E halfway across the 8 cm base, so FE=4. The shaded right triangle has area 4×4√3 divided by 2=8√3.

methods.title: Find the two perpendicular legs
steps: The altitude of the equilateral triangle is 4√3. Thus AF=4√3. Symmetry places E halfway across the 8 cm base, so FE=4. The shaded right triangle has area 4×4√3 divided by 2=8√3.

methods.title: Compare with the equilateral triangle
steps: AFE has the same perpendicular height as AED but half its base length. Its area is half of the equilateral area 8²√3 divided by 4=16√3, hence 8√3.

methods.title: Use an isosceles triangle and parallel lines
steps: Since AD=CD, triangle ADC has equal base angles DAC and ACD, both 2t. Parallel lines give angle ACB=2t too. Hence the whole lower angle C is 4t, and the equal lower angle B is 4t.

methods.title: Use the upper angle first
steps: Triangle ADC has vertex angle ADC=180°−4t. The opposite angle B in an isosceles trapezoid supplements it, giving β=4t.

methods.title: Test an allowed value

explanation: The square diagonal BD=3√2 and makes 45° with BC. Therefore angle DBF=45°+15°=60°. Triangle BDF is right at D, so its short leg BD is half the hypotenuse BF. Thus BF=6√2.

methods.title: Combine the two special triangles
steps: The square diagonal BD=3√2 and makes 45° with BC. Therefore angle DBF=45°+15°=60°. Triangle BDF is right at D, so its short leg BD is half the hypotenuse BF. Thus BF=6√2.

methods.title: Find the longer leg, then apply Pythagoras
steps: The 30°–60°–90° triangle BDF has short leg 3√2, so DF=3√6. Therefore BF²=18+54=72, giving BF=6√2.

geo32-g051.stemHtml: The sum of the lengths of the diagonals of a rhombus is 34 cm. The absolute difference between their lengths is 14 cm. What is its perimeter (in cm)?
explanation: Let the longer diagonal be a. Then a+b=34 and a−b=14, giving a=24 and b=10. Their halves 12 and 5 form a right triangle with side 13. The perimeter is 4×13=52.
geo32-g051.answerHtml: Let the longer diagonal be a. Then a+b=34 and a−b=14, giving a=24 and b=10. Their halves 12 and 5 form a right triangle with side 13. The perimeter is 4×13=52.

methods.title: Find each diagonal, then a side
steps: Let the longer diagonal be a. Then a+b=34 and a−b=14, giving a=24 and b=10. Their halves 12 and 5 form a right triangle with side 13. The perimeter is 4×13=52.

methods.title: Use the sum and difference to find the side squared
steps: The sum of the diagonal squares is (34²+14²) divided by 2=676. A side squared is one quarter of that,169. The side is 13 and the perimeter 52.

geo32-g055.stemHtml: The area of isosceles trapezoid ABCD is 54 cm². DE is an altitude, cm, and the area of triangle DEC is 6 cm². What is AD (in cm)?
explanation: Drop the matching altitude from A. By symmetry both end triangles have area 6. The central rectangle has area 54−12=42 and height 6, so its width AD=7.

methods.title: Use the trapezoid area formula
steps: Triangle DEC gives EC=2. By symmetry the left overhang is 2 as well. If AD=x, BC=x+4. Then ((2x+4)×6) divided by 2=54, so 6x+12=54 and x=7.

geo38-g183.stemRich: ABCD and EFGH are parallelograms. Given: AB = EF = 3 cm, BC = FG = 6 cm, ∠ABC = 75°, and ∠EFG = 45°. Which statement cannot be true?
geo38-g183.stemHtml: ABCD and EFGH are parallelograms. Given: AB = EF = 3 cm, BC = FG = 6 cm, ∠ABC = 75°, and ∠EFG = 45°. Which statement cannot be true?
explanation: Use the 6-cm sides as bases. The 3-cm adjacent side makes a larger acute angle with the base in ABCD, giving a greater height than in EFGH. With equal bases, ABCD has greater area, so equality is impossible.
geo38-g183.answerHtml: Use the 6-cm sides as bases. The 3-cm adjacent side makes a larger acute angle with the base in ABCD, giving a greater height than in EFGH. With equal bases, ABCD has greater area, so equality is impossible.

methods.title: Compare the perpendicular heights
steps: Use the 6-cm sides as bases. The 3-cm adjacent side makes a larger acute angle with the base in ABCD, giving a greater height than in EFGH. With equal bases, ABCD has greater area, so equality is impossible.

methods.title: Eliminate the three necessary truths
steps: Triangle inequality gives AC > 6−3 = 3 = AB. The two triangles defining AC and EG have the same adjacent sides 3 and 6, but 75° > 45°, so AC > EG. Both perimeters are 2(3+6) = 18. The area-equality statement is the only remaining choice.

methods.title: Optional formula check
steps: For adjacent sides a and b and included angle θ, parallelogram area is ab sin θ. The areas are 18 sin 75° and 18 sin 45°. Sine is strictly increasing for acute angles, so the first area is larger.

geo38-g184.stem: KLM is a right triangle with ∠KLM = 90°. N lies on KL, and MN bisects ∠KML. Which of the following statements is necessarily true?
geo38-g184.stemRich: KLM is a right triangle with ∠KLM = 90°. N lies on KL, and MN bisects ∠KML. Which of the following statements is necessarily true?
geo38-g184.stemHtml: KLM is a right triangle with ∠KLM = 90°. N lies on KL, and MN bisects ∠KML. Which of the following statements is necessarily true?
explanation: Drop NE perpendicular to KM. Right triangles MNE and MNL have equal angles at M and common hypotenuse MN, so NE = NL. In right triangle KNE, KN is the hypotenuse and exceeds NE. Thus KN > NL.
geo38-g184.answerHtml: Drop NE perpendicular to KM. Right triangles MNE and MNL have equal angles at M and common hypotenuse MN, so NE = NL. In right triangle KNE, KN is the hypotenuse and exceeds NE. Thus KN > NL.

methods.title: Use equal perpendicular distances from an angle bisector
steps: Drop NE perpendicular to KM. Right triangles MNE and MNL have equal angles at M and common hypotenuse MN, so NE = NL. In right triangle KNE, KN is the hypotenuse and exceeds NE. Thus KN > NL.

methods.title: Use the angle-bisector theorem
steps: The theorem gives $\frac{KN}{NL}=\frac{KM}{ML}$. KM is the hypotenuse of right triangle KLM, so KM > ML. Therefore KN > NL.

methods.title: Eliminate the other statements
steps: Angle MNL is an exterior angle of triangle KMN, so it exceeds angle LKM. Pythagoras gives KM > MN because KL > NL and the other leg ML is shared. Finally, if the half-angle at M is x, angle LKM = 90°−2x, which may be greater than, equal to, or less than x. None of those alternative statements must be true.

geo38-g185.stem: A square and a regular octagon are compared under each of the conditions below. Which statement is false?
geo38-g185.stemRich: A square and a regular octagon are compared under each of the conditions below. Which statement is false?
geo38-g185.stemHtml: A square and a regular octagon are compared under each of the conditions below. Which statement is false?
choices: If both are inscribed in the same circle, the octagon has the greater area.
If both are inscribed in the same circle, the square has the greater perimeter.
If their perimeters are equal, the octagon has the greater area.
If their areas are equal, the square has the greater perimeter.
choicesRich: If both are inscribed in the same circle, the octagon has the greater area.
If both are inscribed in the same circle, the square has the greater perimeter.
If their perimeters are equal, the octagon has the greater area.
If their areas are equal, the square has the greater perimeter.
choicesHtml: If both are inscribed in the same circle, the octagon has the greater area.
If both are inscribed in the same circle, the square has the greater perimeter.
If their perimeters are equal, the octagon has the greater area.
If their areas are equal, the square has the greater perimeter.
explanation: For equal perimeters, a regular octagon encloses more area than a square. For equal areas, it needs less perimeter. For the same circumcircle, the octagon has both greater area and greater perimeter. Thus the claim that the inscribed square has greater perimeter is false.
geo38-g185.answerHtml: For equal perimeters, a regular octagon encloses more area than a square. For equal areas, it needs less perimeter. For the same circumcircle, the octagon has both greater area and greater perimeter. Thus the claim that the inscribed square has greater perimeter is false.

methods.title: Apply the fixed-perimeter and fixed-area comparisons
steps: For equal perimeters, a regular octagon encloses more area than a square. For equal areas, it needs less perimeter. For the same circumcircle, the octagon has both greater area and greater perimeter. Thus the claim that the inscribed square has greater perimeter is false.

methods.title: Compare chords in a common circle
steps: Orient the square so its four vertices are alternate vertices of the octagon. Each square side is replaced along the octagon boundary by two chord segments. By the triangle inequality, those two segments have greater total length than the square side. Summing around the circle proves the octagon perimeter is greater.

geo38-g186.stem: A solid rectangular block is cut into two pieces by one plane passing through its interior. Which of the following cannot be the total number of faces of the two pieces?
geo38-g186.stemRich: A solid rectangular block is cut into two pieces by one plane passing through its interior. Which of the following cannot be the total number of faces of the two pieces?
geo38-g186.stemHtml: A solid rectangular block is cut into two pieces by one plane passing through its interior. Which of the following cannot be the total number of faces of the two pieces?
explanation: Each of the six original faces can contribute at most two faces after the cut, one to each piece. The cut creates exactly two additional faces. The total is therefore at most 6×2+2 = 14, so 15 is impossible.
geo38-g186.answerHtml: Each of the six original faces can contribute at most two faces after the cut, one to each piece. The cut creates exactly two additional faces. The total is therefore at most 6×2+2 = 14, so 15 is impossible.

methods.title: Bound the possible number of faces
steps: Each of the six original faces can contribute at most two faces after the cut, one to each piece. The cut creates exactly two additional faces. The total is therefore at most 6×2+2 = 14, so 15 is impossible.

methods.title: Construct the other three totals
steps: A cut parallel to a face gives two boxes with 6 faces each, total 12. A diagonal cut through two opposite parallel edges gives two triangular prisms with 5 faces each, total 10. Cutting off a corner gives a tetrahedron with 4 faces and a remaining solid with 7, total 11.

geo38-g187.stem: A rectangle tightly contains two rows of n congruent circles of radius r, where n ≥ 2. The circles are arranged in aligned columns and are tangent to their neighbors, as shown in the accompanying figure. How many points of tangency are there between the circles and the sides of the rectangle?
geo38-g187.stemRich: A rectangle tightly contains two rows of n congruent circles of radius r, where n ≥ 2. The circles are arranged in aligned columns and are tangent to their neighbors, as shown in the accompanying figure. How many points of tangency are there between the circles and the sides of the rectangle?
geo38-g187.stemHtml: A rectangle tightly contains two rows of n congruent circles of radius r, where n ≥ 2. The circles are arranged in aligned columns and are tangent to their neighbors, as shown in the accompanying figure. How many points of tangency are there between the circles and the sides of the rectangle?
explanation: The top side touches n circles and the bottom side touches n. The left side touches 2 circles and the right side touches 2. Total: n+n+2+2 = 2n+4. Contacts between circles are not included.
geo38-g187.answerHtml: The top side touches n circles and the bottom side touches n. The left side touches 2 circles and the right side touches 2. Total: n+n+2+2 = 2n+4. Contacts between circles are not included.

methods.title: Count the contacts on the four sides
steps: The top side touches n circles and the bottom side touches n. The left side touches 2 circles and the right side touches 2. Total: n+n+2+2 = 2n+4. Contacts between circles are not included.

methods.title: Count by columns
steps: Each end column contributes 4 boundary contacts, giving 8 altogether. Each of the n−2 interior columns contributes 2, one at the top and one at the bottom. Total: 8+2(n−2) = 2n+4.

methods.title: Test n = 3 to eliminate the choices
steps: For 3 columns, count 3 top, 3 bottom, 2 left and 2 right contacts, total 10. The expressions 2n+4, 2n+2, 4n, and n²+2 give 10, 8, 12, and 11, respectively. Only 2n+4 fits.

geo38-g179.stemRich: AB is a diameter of a circle, and chord CD is perpendicular to AB. The four regions are labeled I, II, III and IV, as shown in the accompanying figure. Ava claims I = II in area. Noah claims II = III. Mia claims I + III = II + IV. Which of the claims are necessarily true?
geo38-g179.stemHtml: AB is a diameter of a circle, and chord CD is perpendicular to AB. The four regions are labeled I, II, III and IV, as shown in the accompanying figure. Ava claims I = II in area. Noah claims II = III. Mia claims I + III = II + IV. Which of the claims are necessarily true?
explanation: Reflection across AB maps region I onto II and IV onto III. Thus I = II and III = IV. Adding gives I+III = II+IV. Region II need not equal III because CD need not be a diameter.
geo38-g179.answerHtml: Reflection across AB maps region I onto II and IV onto III. Thus I = II and III = IV. Adding gives I+III = II+IV. Region II need not equal III because CD need not be a diameter.

methods.title: Move the perpendicular chord
steps: Slide CD toward B while keeping it perpendicular to AB. The left regions remain equal to one another, and the right regions remain equal to one another, but the left pair becomes larger than the right pair. This disproves Noah’s claim while preserving the other two.

geo38-g180.stem: ABCD is a parallelogram, and AC is a diagonal. Given: ∠BAC = 45° and 0° < ∠ABC = β < 80°. Let α = ∠CAD. What is the exact range of α?
geo38-g180.stemRich: ABCD is a parallelogram, and AC is a diagonal. Given: ∠BAC = 45° and 0° < ∠ABC = β < 80°. Let α = ∠CAD. What is the exact range of α?
geo38-g180.stemHtml: ABCD is a parallelogram, and AC is a diagonal. Given: ∠BAC = 45° and 0° < ∠ABC = β < 80°. Let α = ∠CAD. What is the exact range of α?
explanation: At A, the whole angle is α+45°. Adjacent parallelogram angles sum to 180°, so α+45°+β = 180° and α = 135°−β. Since 0°<β<80°, the exact range is 55°<α<135°.
geo38-g180.answerHtml: At A, the whole angle is α+45°. Adjacent parallelogram angles sum to 180°, so α+45°+β = 180° and α = 135°−β. Since 0°<β<80°, the exact range is 55°<α<135°.

methods.title: Use supplementary adjacent angles
steps: At A, the whole angle is α+45°. Adjacent parallelogram angles sum to 180°, so α+45°+β = 180° and α = 135°−β. Since 0°<β<80°, the exact range is 55°<α<135°.

methods.title: Use triangle ABC
steps: Because AD ∥ BC, α equals ∠ACB. The triangle’s angles are 45°, β and α, so α = 135°−β. Checking β near 80° and near 0° gives the strict lower and upper limits.

geo38-g181.stem: Lines a and b are parallel. Segments YZ, WX and UV join them, making acute angles α, β and γ with line a, respectively. Given: α < β < γ < 90°. Which statement cannot be true?
geo38-g181.stemRich: Lines a and b are parallel. Segments YZ, WX and UV join them, making acute angles α, β and γ with line a, respectively. Given: α < β < γ < 90°. Which statement cannot be true?
geo38-g181.stemHtml: Lines a and b are parallel. Segments YZ, WX and UV join them, making acute angles α, β and γ with line a, respectively. Given: α < β < γ < 90°. Which statement cannot be true?
explanation: All three segments cross the same distance between the parallels. A smaller acute angle with the parallel line requires a longer segment. Thus YZ > WX > UV. The statement UV > WX is impossible. VX lies along b, and its length depends on the horizontal spacing of the segments.
geo38-g181.answerHtml: All three segments cross the same distance between the parallels. A smaller acute angle with the parallel line requires a longer segment. Thus YZ > WX > UV. The statement UV > WX is impossible. VX lies along b, and its length depends on the horizontal spacing of the segments.

methods.title: Compare segments across the same perpendicular gap
steps: All three segments cross the same distance between the parallels. A smaller acute angle with the parallel line requires a longer segment. Thus YZ > WX > UV. The statement UV > WX is impossible. VX lies along b, and its length depends on the horizontal spacing of the segments.

methods.title: Use right triangles with equal heights
steps: Drop perpendiculars to b from the three upper endpoints. The resulting right triangles have equal vertical legs. The triangle with the smaller angle at the top parallel has the greater horizontal leg and hence the greater hypotenuse. This gives YZ > WX > UV.

geo38-core-p01.stem: Three circles are externally tangent to one another. Two have radius 2 cm and the third has radius 4 cm. What type of triangle is formed by joining their centers?
geo38-core-p01.stemRich: Three circles are externally tangent to one another. Two have radius 2 cm and the third has radius 4 cm. What type of triangle is formed by joining their centers?
geo38-core-p01.stemHtml: Three circles are externally tangent to one another. Two have radius 2 cm and the third has radius 4 cm. What type of triangle is formed by joining their centers?
explanation: Distances between externally tangent circle centers equal sums of radii. The three sides are 4+2 = 6, 4+2 = 6, and 2+2 = 4. Exactly two sides are equal, so the triangle is isosceles.
geo38-core-p01.answerHtml: Distances between externally tangent circle centers equal sums of radii. The three sides are 4+2 = 6, 4+2 = 6, and 2+2 = 4. Exactly two sides are equal, so the triangle is isosceles.

methods.title: Add the radii at each tangency
steps: Distances between externally tangent circle centers equal sums of radii. The three sides are 4+2 = 6, 4+2 = 6, and 2+2 = 4. Exactly two sides are equal, so the triangle is isosceles.

methods.title: Use the equal-circle symmetry
steps: The center of the 4-cm circle is the same distance from each 2-cm circle’s center. Those equal center distances are the two equal sides. The remaining side is shorter, so the triangle is not equilateral.

geo38-core-p02.stem: ABCD and DEFG are squares. E lies on DC, and their top sides AD and DG lie on one straight line. Given: FG = 2 cm. What is CF?
geo38-core-p02.stemRich: ABCD and DEFG are squares. E lies on DC, and their top sides AD and DG lie on one straight line. Given: FG = 2 cm. What is CF?
geo38-core-p02.stemHtml: ABCD and DEFG are squares. E lies on DC, and their top sides AD and DG lie on one straight line. Given: FG = 2 cm. What is CF?
choices: It cannot be determined from the information given.
choicesRich: It cannot be determined from the information given.
choicesHtml: It cannot be determined from the information given.
explanation: The small square fixes EF = 2, but EC equals the larger square’s side minus 2 and is not given. Since CF is the hypotenuse of right triangle CEF, its length changes with EC.
geo38-core-p02.answerHtml: The small square fixes EF = 2, but EC equals the larger square’s side minus 2 and is not given. Since CF is the hypotenuse of right triangle CEF, its length changes with EC.

methods.title: Identify the missing larger-square side
steps: The small square fixes EF = 2, but EC equals the larger square’s side minus 2 and is not given. Since CF is the hypotenuse of right triangle CEF, its length changes with EC.

methods.title: Give two permitted examples
steps: If the large square has side 4, then EC = 2 and CF = 2√2. If its side is 6, then EC = 4 and CF = 2√5. Both satisfy the conditions and give different answers.

geo38-core-p03.stemRich: A, C and E lie on line k. AB, CD and EF are perpendicular to k, and ∠BDF = 90°. Which of the following statements is necessarily true?
geo38-core-p03.stemHtml: A, C and E lie on line k. AB, CD and EF are perpendicular to k, and ∠BDF = 90°. Which of the following statements is necessarily true?
choices: None of the above is necessarily true.
choicesRich: None of the above is necessarily true.
choicesHtml: None of the above is necessarily true.
explanation: Take A(0,7), C(0,3), E(0,0), B(4,7), D(2,3), and F(8,0). The three horizontal segments are perpendicular to k. DB has direction (2,4), and DF has direction (6,−3), which are perpendicular. But AB = 4 ≠ 8 = EF, AC = 4 ≠ 3 = CE, and BD = √20 ≠ √45 = DF.
geo38-core-p03.answerHtml: Take A(0,7), C(0,3), E(0,0), B(4,7), D(2,3), and F(8,0). The three horizontal segments are perpendicular to k. DB has direction (2,4), and DF has direction (6,−3), which are perpendicular. But AB = 4 ≠ 8 = EF, AC = 4 ≠ 3 = CE, and BD = √20 ≠ √45 = DF.

methods.title: Use one counterexample to test all three equalities
steps: Take A(0,7), C(0,3), E(0,0), B(4,7), D(2,3), and F(8,0). The three horizontal segments are perpendicular to k. DB has direction (2,4), and DF has direction (6,−3), which are perpendicular. But AB = 4 ≠ 8 = EF, AC = 4 ≠ 3 = CE, and BD = √20 ≠ √45 = DF.

methods.title: Notice what the right angle does and does not fix
steps: The right angle at D fixes an angle between BD and DF. It does not state that this right triangle is isosceles, or that C is the midpoint of AE, or that the outer horizontal segments are equal. The valid unequal construction shows that none of those extra symmetries is forced.

methods.title: Subtract the common angle from two right angles

methods.title: Use the rotation of perpendicular ray pairs

geo38-core-p05.stemHtml: In acute triangle ABC, D is the point on BC closest to A. Which of the following statements is necessarily true?
explanation: The shortest distance from a point to a line is measured along a perpendicular. Since the triangle is acute, the perpendicular foot lies inside BC, so AD ⟂ BC.
geo38-core-p05.answerHtml: The shortest distance from a point to a line is measured along a perpendicular. Since the triangle is acute, the perpendicular foot lies inside BC, so AD ⟂ BC.

methods.title: Use the shortest-distance property
steps: The shortest distance from a point to a line is measured along a perpendicular. Since the triangle is acute, the perpendicular foot lies inside BC, so AD ⟂ BC.

methods.title: Compare other points using Pythagoras
steps: Let H be the perpendicular foot from A to BC. For any other point X on BC, AX² = AH²+HX² > AH². Thus H is the unique closest point and must be D. No midpoint or angle-bisector property follows.

explanation: CA = CB. A traces the upper-left quarter circle and B traces the upper-right quarter circle, both centered at C with the same radius. Together they form the upper semicircle.

geo38-core-p07.stem: A square sheet with side 12 cm is cut into two pieces by one straight cut. Which pair of shapes cannot be obtained?
geo38-core-p07.stemRich: A square sheet with side 12 cm is cut into two pieces by one straight cut. Which pair of shapes cannot be obtained?
geo38-core-p07.stemHtml: A square sheet with side 12 cm is cut into two pieces by one straight cut. Which pair of shapes cannot be obtained?
choices: Two trapezoids, each with exactly one pair of parallel sides
choicesRich: Two trapezoids, each with exactly one pair of parallel sides
choicesHtml: Two trapezoids, each with exactly one pair of parallel sides
explanation: A diagonal gives two triangles. A slanted cut joining opposite sides gives two trapezoids. A cut parallel to a side gives two rectangles. For two quadrilaterals, the cut must join opposite sides, and each piece keeps two right-angle corners. A rhombus with a right angle is a square, so neither piece can be a non-square rhombus.
geo38-core-p07.answerHtml: A diagonal gives two triangles. A slanted cut joining opposite sides gives two trapezoids. A cut parallel to a side gives two rectangles. For two quadrilaterals, the cut must join opposite sides, and each piece keeps two right-angle corners. A rhombus with a right angle is a square, so neither piece can be a non-square rhombus.

methods.title: Classify the cut positions
steps: A diagonal gives two triangles. A slanted cut joining opposite sides gives two trapezoids. A cut parallel to a side gives two rectangles. For two quadrilaterals, the cut must join opposite sides, and each piece keeps two right-angle corners. A rhombus with a right angle is a square, so neither piece can be a non-square rhombus.

methods.title: Use the angles inherited from the sheet
steps: One straight cut cannot remove all four square corners from two quadrilateral pieces. Each quadrilateral retains right angles. Non-square rhombi have no right angles, so the proposed pair is impossible.

steps: AC bisects BD at right angles, so each half of BD is 3. But the two parts of AC need not be equal. The side lengths depend on those separate parts, which the question does not give.

methods.title: Construct two kites with the same diagonals
steps: If AC is split into 4 and 6, the perimeter is 2√(4²+3²)+2√(6²+3²) = 10+6√5. If it is split into 2 and 8, the perimeter is 2√13+2√73. These differ, while the full diagonals remain 10 and 6.

geo38-core-p09.stemRich: ABC is right-angled at B. AD bisects ∠BAC, with D on BC. E lies on AC and DE ⟂ AC. Which of the following statements is necessarily true?
geo38-core-p09.stemHtml: ABC is right-angled at B. AD bisects ∠BAC, with D on BC. E lies on AC and DE ⟂ AC. Which of the following statements is necessarily true?
explanation: Right triangles ABD and AED share hypotenuse AD and have equal angles at A, so they are congruent. Thus AB = AE and BD = DE. In right triangle DEC, DC is the hypotenuse and exceeds DE, so BD < DC.
geo38-core-p09.answerHtml: Right triangles ABD and AED share hypotenuse AD and have equal angles at A, so they are congruent. Thus AB = AE and BD = DE. In right triangle DEC, DC is the hypotenuse and exceeds DE, so BD < DC.

methods.title: Use congruent right triangles and a hypotenuse comparison
steps: Right triangles ABD and AED share hypotenuse AD and have equal angles at A, so they are congruent. Thus AB = AE and BD = DE. In right triangle DEC, DC is the hypotenuse and exceeds DE, so BD < DC.

methods.title: Combine reflection and the angle-bisector theorem
steps: Reflection across AD maps the perpendicular feet B and E to each other, so AB = AE. The angle-bisector theorem gives BD : DC = AB : AC. Since AC is the hypotenuse, AB < AC, so BD < DC.

geo38-core-p12.stem: Chords AC and BD of a circle intersect perpendicularly at E, and AE = EC. Region I is the part of the disk above BD and to the right of AC. Region II is below BD and to the left of AC. Which of the following statements is necessarily true?
geo38-core-p12.stemRich: Chords AC and BD of a circle intersect perpendicularly at E, and AE = EC. Region I is the part of the disk above BD and to the right of AC. Region II is below BD and to the left of AC. Which of the following statements is necessarily true?
geo38-core-p12.stemHtml: Chords AC and BD of a circle intersect perpendicularly at E, and AE = EC. Region I is the part of the disk above BD and to the right of AC. Region II is below BD and to the left of AC. Which of the following statements is necessarily true?
choices: None of the other statements is necessarily true.
choicesRich: None of the other statements is necessarily true.
choicesHtml: None of the other statements is necessarily true.
explanation: Since BD is the perpendicular bisector of AC, it passes through the center. But E need not be the center. If AC lies right of the center, I is smaller than II; if it lies left, I is larger; if both are diameters, they are equal.
geo38-core-p12.answerHtml: Since BD is the perpendicular bisector of AC, it passes through the center. But E need not be the center. If AC lies right of the center, I is smaller than II; if it lies left, I is larger; if both are diameters, they are equal.

methods.title: The perpendicular bisector identifies one diameter, not the center of both chords
steps: Since BD is the perpendicular bisector of AC, it passes through the center. But E need not be the center. If AC lies right of the center, I is smaller than II; if it lies left, I is larger; if both are diameters, they are equal.

methods.title: Reflect across BD and compare the two sides of AC
steps: Reflection across the diameter BD preserves each left-or-right disk portion, so II equals the upper-left portion. The comparison with upper-right region I therefore depends on where AC lies relative to the center. That position is unspecified.

ntTerminology: logic: "must be true" -> "is necessarily true" (stem and none-choice; choice is not last so "other" kept)

geo38-core-p13.stem: ABCD is a rhombus with ∠ABC = 40°. EFGH is a square, and AB = EF = 4 cm. Which of the following statements is necessarily true?
geo38-core-p13.stemRich: ABCD is a rhombus with ∠ABC = 40°. EFGH is a square, and AB = EF = 4 cm. Which of the following statements is necessarily true?
geo38-core-p13.stemHtml: ABCD is a rhombus with ∠ABC = 40°. EFGH is a square, and AB = EF = 4 cm. Which of the following statements is necessarily true?
choices: The square has greater area than the rhombus.
The square has greater perimeter than the rhombus.
choicesRich: The square has greater area than the rhombus.
The square has greater perimeter than the rhombus.
choicesHtml: The square has greater area than the rhombus.
The square has greater perimeter than the rhombus.
explanation: The square has base 4 and height 4. The rhombus has base 4, but its sloping side of length 4 gives a perpendicular height strictly below 4. Its area is therefore less than 16.
geo38-core-p13.answerHtml: The square has base 4 and height 4. The rhombus has base 4, but its sloping side of length 4 gives a perpendicular height strictly below 4. Its area is therefore less than 16.

methods.title: Compare heights at the same base length
steps: The square has base 4 and height 4. The rhombus has base 4, but its sloping side of length 4 gives a perpendicular height strictly below 4. Its area is therefore less than 16.

methods.title: Use the fixed-perimeter maximum for quadrilaterals
steps: Both perimeters are 16. Among quadrilaterals with that perimeter, the square has greatest area. The given 40° angle makes the rhombus non-square, so its area is strictly smaller.

methods.title: Eliminate the other claims
steps: In isosceles triangle ABC, the base angles are 70°, so AC, opposite 40°, is less than AB. The perimeters are equal. The rhombus’s long diagonal BD is opposite a 140° angle between equal sides, whereas square diagonal EG is opposite 90°, so BD > EG.

geo38-core-p14.stem: KN is a median of triangle KLM, and P lies strictly between K and N. Let α = ∠LPN and β = ∠LKP. Which of the following is necessarily true?
geo38-core-p14.stemRich: KN is a median of triangle KLM, and P lies strictly between K and N. Let α = ∠LPN and β = ∠LKP. Which of the following is necessarily true?
geo38-core-p14.stemHtml: KN is a median of triangle KLM, and P lies strictly between K and N. Let α = ∠LPN and β = ∠LKP. Which of the following is necessarily true?
choices: It cannot be determined from the information given.
choicesRich: It cannot be determined from the information given.
choicesHtml: It cannot be determined from the information given.
explanation: PN extends PK beyond P. Thus α is an exterior angle of triangle KLP and equals β + ∠KLP. The added angle is positive, so α > β.
geo38-core-p14.answerHtml: PN extends PK beyond P. Thus α is an exterior angle of triangle KLP and equals β + ∠KLP. The added angle is positive, so α > β.

methods.title: Use the exterior-angle theorem
steps: PN extends PK beyond P. Thus α is an exterior angle of triangle KLP and equals β + ∠KLP. The added angle is positive, so α > β.

methods.title: Subtract the interior angle at P from 180°
steps: In triangle KLP, β+∠KLP+∠KPL = 180°. Also α+∠KPL = 180°. Equating gives α = β+∠KLP > β. The median condition is more information than this comparison needs.

geo38-core-p15.stem: A drawing contains 5 horizontal segments on distinct lines and 8 vertical segments on distinct lines. The segments may be placed and given lengths freely. Which describes all possible numbers of intersection points?
geo38-core-p15.stemRich: A drawing contains 5 horizontal segments on distinct lines and 8 vertical segments on distinct lines. The segments may be placed and given lengths freely. Which describes all possible numbers of intersection points?
geo38-core-p15.stemHtml: A drawing contains 5 horizontal segments on distinct lines and 8 vertical segments on distinct lines. The segments may be placed and given lengths freely. Which describes all possible numbers of intersection points?
explanation: Each of the 5 horizontal segments can meet at most 8 vertical segments, so the maximum is 40. Separating the groups gives 0. For any count 8q+r with 0≤r<8, let q horizontal segments cross all 8 verticals, one more cross exactly r, and the rest cross none. The case 40 uses all 5 full rows.
geo38-core-p15.answerHtml: Each of the 5 horizontal segments can meet at most 8 vertical segments, so the maximum is 40. Separating the groups gives 0. For any count 8q+r with 0≤r<8, let q horizontal segments cross all 8 verticals, one more cross exactly r, and the rest cross none. The case 40 uses all 5 full rows.

methods.title: Find the bounds and construct each intermediate count
steps: Each of the 5 horizontal segments can meet at most 8 vertical segments, so the maximum is 40. Separating the groups gives 0. For any count 8q+r with 0≤r<8, let q horizontal segments cross all 8 verticals, one more cross exactly r, and the rest cross none. The case 40 uses all 5 full rows.

methods.title: Count one adjustable row at a time
steps: Make all vertical segments long enough to reach the five distinct horizontal levels. By choosing each horizontal segment’s endpoint, it can meet any number from 0 through 8 of the verticals. The sum of five such counts can be any integer from 0 through 40.

geo38-core-p16.stem: ABCD is a parallelogram with BC = 5 cm. A right isosceles triangle AEB is constructed externally on AB, with right angle E and area 18 cm². What is the area of the parallelogram?
geo38-core-p16.stemRich: ABCD is a parallelogram with BC = 5 cm. A right isosceles triangle AEB is constructed externally on AB, with right angle E and area 18 cm². What is the area of the parallelogram?
geo38-core-p16.stemHtml: ABCD is a parallelogram with BC = 5 cm. A right isosceles triangle AEB is constructed externally on AB, with right angle E and area 18 cm². What is the area of the parallelogram?
choices: It cannot be determined from the information given.
choicesRich: It cannot be determined from the information given.
choicesHtml: It cannot be determined from the information given.
explanation: The equal triangle legs satisfy l² divided by 2 = 18, so l = 6 and AB = 6√2. The parallelogram has fixed sides 5 and 6√2, but its included angle is unspecified. Its height and area can vary.
geo38-core-p16.answerHtml: The equal triangle legs satisfy l² divided by 2 = 18, so l = 6 and AB = 6√2. The parallelogram has fixed sides 5 and 6√2, but its included angle is unspecified. Its height and area can vary.

methods.title: The triangle fixes a side, but not the parallelogram’s height
steps: The equal triangle legs satisfy l² divided by 2 = 18, so l = 6 and AB = 6√2. The parallelogram has fixed sides 5 and 6√2, but its included angle is unspecified. Its height and area can vary.

methods.title: Construct two permitted angles
steps: If the parallelogram’s angle between AB and BC is 90°, its area is 30√2. If that angle is 45°, its perpendicular height is 6 and its area is 30. The same external right isosceles triangle can be attached to AB in either case.

geo38-core-p17.stem: A, B, C and D lie on one circle. The minor arc CD is 3 times the minor arc AB. P and Q may be any points strictly inside the circle, and need not be distinct. Let α = ∠APB and β = ∠CQD. Which of the following is necessarily true?
geo38-core-p17.stemRich: A, B, C and D lie on one circle. The minor arc CD is 3 times the minor arc AB. P and Q may be any points strictly inside the circle, and need not be distinct. Let α = ∠APB and β = ∠CQD. Which of the following is necessarily true?
geo38-core-p17.stemHtml: A, B, C and D lie on one circle. The minor arc CD is 3 times the minor arc AB. P and Q may be any points strictly inside the circle, and need not be distinct. Let α = ∠APB and β = ∠CQD. Which of the following is necessarily true?
choices: None of the other relationships is necessarily true.
choicesRich: None of the other relationships is necessarily true.
choicesHtml: None of the other relationships is necessarily true.
explanation: Choose arcs AB = 20° and CD = 60°. With both vertices at the center, α = 20° and β = 60°, so equality holds. Keeping Q at the center and moving P close to the midpoint of chord AB makes α approach 180°, giving β < 3α. Keeping P at the center and moving Q close to chord CD makes β approach 180°, giving β > 3α. All vertices can remain strictly inside the disk.
geo38-core-p17.answerHtml: Choose arcs AB = 20° and CD = 60°. With both vertices at the center, α = 20° and β = 60°, so equality holds. Keeping Q at the center and moving P close to the midpoint of chord AB makes α approach 180°, giving β < 3α. Keeping P at the center and moving Q close to chord CD makes β approach 180°, giving β > 3α. All vertices can remain strictly inside the disk.

methods.title: Compare a central case with moved vertices
steps: Choose arcs AB = 20° and CD = 60°. With both vertices at the center, α = 20° and β = 60°, so equality holds. Keeping Q at the center and moving P close to the midpoint of chord AB makes α approach 180°, giving β < 3α. Keeping P at the center and moving Q close to chord CD makes β approach 180°, giving β > 3α. All vertices can remain strictly inside the disk.

methods.title: Check which angle theorem applies
steps: Arc measure controls a central angle directly and an inscribed angle by a factor of one half. These angles have freely placed interior vertices, so neither rule fixes their ratio. The legal center-and-move examples demonstrate the missing restriction.

geo38-core-p19.stemRich: How many mutually noncongruent rhombi have perimeter 28 cm and area 35 cm²?
geo38-core-p19.stemHtml: How many mutually noncongruent rhombi have perimeter 28 cm and area 35 cm²?
explanation: Every side is 7. The area formula gives height h = 35 : 7 = 5. A sloping side of length 7 with vertical component 5 has horizontal component √(49−25) = 2√6. This fixes the rhombus up to reflection and rotation, which preserve congruence.
geo38-core-p19.answerHtml: Every side is 7. The area formula gives height h = 35 : 7 = 5. A sloping side of length 7 with vertical component 5 has horizontal component √(49−25) = 2√6. This fixes the rhombus up to reflection and rotation, which preserve congruence.

methods.title: Fix the side and perpendicular height
steps: Every side is 7. The area formula gives height h = 35 : 7 = 5. A sloping side of length 7 with vertical component 5 has horizontal component √(49−25) = 2√6. This fixes the rhombus up to reflection and rotation, which preserve congruence.

methods.title: Use the acute angle determined by side and height
steps: The height-to-side ratio is 5 : 7, fixing one acute angle. Choosing its supplementary angle produces the same rhombus with the vertices relabeled. Since 0<35<49, a nondegenerate rhombus exists, and there is exactly one congruence class.

explanation: The largest rectangle area for a fixed perimeter occurs at a square. Each side is 36 : 4 = 9, so the greatest area is 81.

methods.title: Use the square as the maximizing rectangle
steps: The largest rectangle area for a fixed perimeter occurs at a square. Each side is 36 : 4 = 9, so the greatest area is 81.

methods.title: Complete the square in the area expression
steps: If one side is x, the other is 18−x. Area = x(18−x) = 81−(x−9)², which cannot exceed 81 and reaches it at x = 9.

methods.title: Count and reject the degenerate endpoints
steps: There are 11 integers from 2 through 12, inclusive. Lengths 2 and 12 make the triangle collapse into a straight line, so remove both, leaving 9.

geo38-core-p27.stem: Two disks each have radius 3 cm, and their centers are 4 cm apart. Let A be the area covered by at least one disk. Which of the following statements is necessarily true?
geo38-core-p27.stemRich: Two disks each have radius 3 cm, and their centers are 4 cm apart. Let A be the area covered by at least one disk. Which of the following statements is necessarily true?
geo38-core-p27.stemHtml: Two disks each have radius 3 cm, and their centers are 4 cm apart. Let A be the area covered by at least one disk. Which of the following statements is necessarily true?
explanation: The center distance 4 is less than the sum of radii 6, so the disks overlap in positive area. Their union is therefore less than the sum 18π. Their centers differ and neither equal disk contains the other, so their union is greater than one disk’s area 9π.
geo38-core-p27.answerHtml: The center distance 4 is less than the sum of radii 6, so the disks overlap in positive area. Their union is therefore less than the sum 18π. Their centers differ and neither equal disk contains the other, so their union is greater than one disk’s area 9π.

methods.title: Use overlap and containment
steps: The center distance 4 is less than the sum of radii 6, so the disks overlap in positive area. Their union is therefore less than the sum 18π. Their centers differ and neither equal disk contains the other, so their union is greater than one disk’s area 9π.

methods.title: Use the inclusion-exclusion formula
steps: If I is the overlap area, then A = 18π−I. The geometry gives 0<I<9π: there is genuine overlap, but the disks are not identical. Subtracting gives 9π<A<18π.

geo36-g148.stemRich: D and F are the midpoints of sides AB and AC of triangle ABC, respectively. The area of trapezoid DBCF is 15 cm². What is the area of triangle ADF (in cm²)?
geo36-g148.stemHtml: D and F are the midpoints of sides AB and AC of triangle ABC, respectively. The area of trapezoid DBCF is 15 cm². What is the area of triangle ADF (in cm²)?
explanation: DF ∥ BC and triangle ADF is similar to ABC with length ratio 1 : 2. Its area is one quarter of the whole, while the trapezoid is three quarters. Small triangle : trapezoid = 1 : 3, so the triangle area is 15 : 3 = 5.
geo36-g148.answerHtml: DF ∥ BC and triangle ADF is similar to ABC with length ratio 1 : 2. Its area is one quarter of the whole, while the trapezoid is three quarters. Small triangle : trapezoid = 1 : 3, so the triangle area is 15 : 3 = 5.

methods.title: Use the midpoint length and area ratios
steps: DF ∥ BC and triangle ADF is similar to ABC with length ratio 1 : 2. Its area is one quarter of the whole, while the trapezoid is three quarters. Small triangle : trapezoid = 1 : 3, so the triangle area is 15 : 3 = 5.

methods.title: Divide the whole triangle into four congruent triangles
steps: Join D and F to the midpoint M of BC. The four small triangles have the same three side lengths, half the original sides, so they are congruent. The trapezoid contains three of them. Each has area 15 : 3 = 5, including ADF.

methods.title: Use the triangle and trapezoid formulas
steps: Let DF = b and the small triangle height be h. Then BC = 2b and the trapezoid height is h. Its area is $\frac{(b+2b)h}{2}=15$, giving bh = 10. The small triangle area is $\frac{bh}{2}=5$.

geo36-g149.stem: Two regular hexagons have areas 72\sqrt3 cm² and 24\sqrt3 cm². What is the ratio of the perimeter of the first hexagon to the perimeter of the second?
geo36-g149.stemRich: Two regular hexagons have areas $72\sqrt3$ cm² and $24\sqrt3$ cm². What is the ratio of the perimeter of the first hexagon to the perimeter of the second?
geo36-g149.stemHtml: Two regular hexagons have areas cm² and cm². What is the ratio of the perimeter of the first hexagon to the perimeter of the second?
explanation: The two regular hexagons are similar. Their area ratio is 72√3 : 24√3 = 3 : 1. The perimeter ratio is the corresponding length ratio, √3 : 1.
geo36-g149.answerHtml: The two regular hexagons are similar. Their area ratio is 72√3 : 24√3 = 3 : 1. The perimeter ratio is the corresponding length ratio, √3 : 1.

methods.title: Take the square root of the area ratio
steps: The two regular hexagons are similar. Their area ratio is 72√3 : 24√3 = 3 : 1. The perimeter ratio is the corresponding length ratio, √3 : 1.

methods.title: Find the two side lengths
steps: A regular hexagon has area $\frac{3\sqrt3}{2}s^2$. For the first, $s^2=48$, so $s=4\sqrt3$. For the second, $s^2=16$, so s = 4. Their perimeters are $24\sqrt3$ and 24, giving ratio $\sqrt3:1$.

methods.title: Cancel the common hexagon area constant
steps: Write the areas as $Ks_1^2$ and $Ks_2^2$, where $K=\frac{3\sqrt3}{2}$. Their ratio gives $\frac{s_1^2}{s_2^2}=3$, so $\frac{s_1}{s_2}=\sqrt3$. Multiplying both sides by six to obtain perimeters leaves that ratio unchanged.

geo36-g150.stemRich: A spherical display contains a smaller solid ball. The smaller ball’s diameter is $\frac23$ of the larger sphere’s radius. What is the ratio of the difference between their volumes to the smaller ball’s volume?
geo36-g150.stemHtml: A spherical display contains a smaller solid ball. The smaller ball’s diameter is of the larger sphere’s radius. What is the ratio of the difference between their volumes to the smaller ball’s volume?
explanation: If the large radius is R, the small diameter is 2R divided by 3, so the small radius is R divided by 3. The volume ratio small : large is 1 : 27. Their difference is 26 small-volume units, giving 26 : 1.
geo36-g150.answerHtml: If the large radius is R, the small diameter is 2R divided by 3, so the small radius is R divided by 3. The volume ratio small : large is 1 : 27. Their difference is 26 small-volume units, giving 26 : 1.

methods.title: Convert to corresponding radii, then cube
steps: If the large radius is R, the small diameter is 2R divided by 3, so the small radius is R divided by 3. The volume ratio small : large is 1 : 27. Their difference is 26 small-volume units, giving 26 : 1.

methods.title: Use the sphere-volume formula as an optional check
steps: With small radius r, the large radius is 3r. The volumes are $\frac43\pi r^3$ and $\frac43\pi(3r)^3=27(\frac43\pi r^3)$. Subtract one small volume, leaving 26 of them.

geo36-g151.stem: A cone-shaped tank with base radius r and height h is filled with water using a cone-shaped measuring cup. The cup’s radius is \frac r3 and its height is \frac h4. How many full cups are needed to fill the tank, assuming all the water is transferred without loss?
geo36-g151.stemRich: A cone-shaped tank with base radius r and height h is filled with water using a cone-shaped measuring cup. The cup’s radius is $\frac r3$ and its height is $\frac h4$. How many full cups are needed to fill the tank, assuming all the water is transferred without loss?
geo36-g151.stemHtml: A cone-shaped tank with base radius r and height h is filled with water using a cone-shaped measuring cup. The cup’s radius is and its height is . How many full cups are needed to fill the tank, assuming all the water is transferred without loss?
explanation: From cup to tank, the radius is multiplied by 3, so base area is multiplied by 9. Height is multiplied by 4. Both shapes are cones, so the common one-third factor cancels. Volume factor = 9×4 = 36.
geo36-g151.answerHtml: From cup to tank, the radius is multiplied by 3, so base area is multiplied by 9. Height is multiplied by 4. Both shapes are cones, so the common one-third factor cancels. Volume factor = 9×4 = 36.

methods.title: Combine the radius and height factors
steps: From cup to tank, the radius is multiplied by 3, so base area is multiplied by 9. Height is multiplied by 4. Both shapes are cones, so the common one-third factor cancels. Volume factor = 9×4 = 36.

methods.title: Divide the volume formulas
steps: The tank volume is $\frac{\pi r^2h}{3}$. The cup volume is $\frac{\pi(r:3)^2(h:4)}3=\frac{\pi r^2h}{108}$. The tank holds 36 cup volumes.

methods.title: Choose convenient dimensions
steps: Let r = 3 and h = 12. The tank volume is 36π. The cup has radius 1 and height 3, so its volume is π. It takes 36 such cups.

geo36-g144.stem: In triangle ABC, D lies on BC and E lies on AC. Given: ED ∥ AB, BD = 4 cm, DC = 8 cm, and AE = 5 cm. What is AC (in cm)?
geo36-g144.stemRich: In triangle ABC, D lies on BC and E lies on AC. Given: ED ∥ AB, BD = 4 cm, DC = 8 cm, and AE = 5 cm. What is AC (in cm)?
geo36-g144.stemHtml: In triangle ABC, D lies on BC and E lies on AC. Given: ED ∥ AB, BD = 4 cm, DC = 8 cm, and AE = 5 cm. What is AC (in cm)?
explanation: Triangles EDC and ABC are similar. Their scale factor is DC : BC = 8 : 12 = 2 : 3. Thus EC is two thirds of AC and AE is one third of AC. Since AE = 5, AC = 15.
geo36-g144.answerHtml: Triangles EDC and ABC are similar. Their scale factor is DC : BC = 8 : 12 = 2 : 3. Thus EC is two thirds of AC and AE is one third of AC. Since AE = 5, AC = 15.

methods.title: Compare the whole and small triangles
steps: Triangles EDC and ABC are similar. Their scale factor is DC : BC = 8 : 12 = 2 : 3. Thus EC is two thirds of AC and AE is one third of AC. Since AE = 5, AC = 15.

methods.title: Use an equation for the unknown small side
steps: Let EC = x. Then AC = x + 5 and $\frac8{12}=\frac{x}{x+5}$. Cross-multiply: $8x+40=12x$, so x = 10 and AC = 15.

methods.title: Use the corresponding side partitions
steps: A parallel cut divides the two sides in the same ratio. BD : DC = 4 : 8 = 1 : 2, so AE : EC = 1 : 2. With AE = 5, EC = 10 and AC = 15.

geo36-g145.stemHtml: ABC is a right triangle with right angle C. DECF is a square, D lies on AB, and AF = 3 cm. If the square’s side is x cm, what is BE (in cm)?
explanation: Triangles AFD and DEB are similar. The matching legs give $\frac{AF}{DE}=\frac{FD}{EB}$, so $\frac3x=\frac{x}{BE}$. Hence $BE=\frac{x^2}{3}$.

methods.title: Choose a valid value that separates the choices

geo36-g146.stem: ABC is a right triangle with right angle A. AD is perpendicular to BC, BD = 9 cm, and DC = 16 cm. What is AD (in cm)?
geo36-g146.stemRich: ABC is a right triangle with right angle A. AD is perpendicular to BC, BD = 9 cm, and DC = 16 cm. What is AD (in cm)?
geo36-g146.stemHtml: ABC is a right triangle with right angle A. AD is perpendicular to BC, BD = 9 cm, and DC = 16 cm. What is AD (in cm)?
explanation: Triangles ABD and CAD are similar. Their matching legs give $\frac{BD}{AD}=\frac{AD}{DC}$. Thus $AD^2=9\times16=144$, and AD = 12.
geo36-g146.answerHtml: Triangles ABD and CAD are similar. Their matching legs give . Thus , and AD = 12.

methods.title: Use similarity between the two smaller triangles
steps: Triangles ABD and CAD are similar. Their matching legs give $\frac{BD}{AD}=\frac{AD}{DC}$. Thus $AD^2=9\times16=144$, and AD = 12.

methods.title: Use the altitude-to-hypotenuse relationship
steps: The altitude to a right triangle’s hypotenuse is the geometric mean of the two pieces it creates. Therefore AD = √(9×16) = 12. This relationship follows from the similarity proportion above.

methods.title: Use the Pythagorean theorem in all three triangles
steps: Let AD = h. Then AB² = h² + 81 and AC² = h² + 256. Since BC = 25 and angle A is right, AB² + AC² = 625. Thus 2h² + 337 = 625, giving h² = 144 and h = 12.

geo36-core-p02.stemHtml: A, B, C, D and E lie on one straight line, with AB = BC = CD = DE. F and G lie on a ray from A, and EF and CG are perpendicular to AE. What is CG : EF?
explanation: Triangles ACG and AEF share angle A and have right angles at C and E. Their length ratio is AC : AE = 2 : 4 = 1 : 2. Therefore CG : EF = 1 : 2.
geo36-core-p02.answerHtml: Triangles ACG and AEF share angle A and have right angles at C and E. Their length ratio is AC : AE = 2 : 4 = 1 : 2. Therefore CG : EF = 1 : 2.

methods.title: Use a midpoint segment
steps: C is the midpoint of AE. The segment through C parallel to EF meets AF at its midpoint G, and is half EF. Thus CG : EF = 1 : 2.

explanation: Triangles EAD and DCF are similar. Their matching legs give $\frac{AE}{DC}=\frac{AD}{CF}$. Hence AD×DC = AE×CF = 3×5 = 15, exactly the rectangle area.

steps: Let rectangle width be w and height h. Triangle EBF has area $\frac12(w+5)(h+3)$. It also consists of the rectangle plus two triangles, giving $wh+\frac32w+\frac52h$. Equating and simplifying gives wh = 15.

explanation: AG = 5 and AB = 10, so AG is half the hypotenuse in triangle AGB. By similarity, AF is half AC = 14, hence AF = 7. The Pythagorean theorem gives CF² = 14² − 7² = 147. That is the requested square’s area; no square root is needed.

methods.title: Recognize the special right triangles
steps: In AGB, the hypotenuse is twice leg AG, so it is a 30°–60°–90° triangle. The similar large triangle has hypotenuse 14 and short leg 7, so its long leg CF is 7√3. The square area is (7√3)² = 147.

geo36-g137.stemRich: AB is a diameter of a circle with radius 7 cm. Four congruent smaller circles have their centers on AB. Their diameters partition AB without gaps, as shown in the accompanying figure. What is the sum of the circumferences of the four smaller circles (in cm)?
geo36-g137.stemHtml: AB is a diameter of a circle with radius 7 cm. Four congruent smaller circles have their centers on AB. Their diameters partition AB without gaps, as shown in the accompanying figure. What is the sum of the circumferences of the four smaller circles (in cm)?
explanation: Each small diameter is one fourth of AB, so each small circumference is one fourth of the large circumference. Four such circumferences sum to the large circumference, 2π×7 = 14π.
geo36-g137.answerHtml: Each small diameter is one fourth of AB, so each small circumference is one fourth of the large circumference. Four such circumferences sum to the large circumference, 2π×7 = 14π.

methods.title: Use the common length ratio
steps: Each small diameter is one fourth of AB, so each small circumference is one fourth of the large circumference. Four such circumferences sum to the large circumference, 2π×7 = 14π.

methods.title: Calculate one small radius
steps: The large diameter is 14. Each small diameter is $\frac{14}{4}=\frac72$, so each radius is $\frac74$. Four circumferences total $4\times2\pi\times\frac74=14\pi$.

methods.title: Add the diameters before multiplying by π
steps: For every circle, circumference equals π times diameter. Since the four small diameters sum to 14, their circumferences sum to π×14 = 14π. This also works for unequal small circles whose diameters partition AB.

geo36-g140.stemHtml: In triangle ABC, D lies on AB and E lies on AC. Given: DE ∥ BC, AD = 3 cm, and DB = 2 cm. What is the ratio of the area of triangle ADE to the area of trapezoid DBCE?

geo36-g142.stem: The area of one face of a large cube is 16 times the area of one face of a small cube. How many such small cubes can fill the large cube completely?
geo36-g142.stemRich: The area of one face of a large cube is 16 times the area of one face of a small cube. How many such small cubes can fill the large cube completely?
geo36-g142.stemHtml: The area of one face of a large cube is 16 times the area of one face of a small cube. How many such small cubes can fill the large cube completely?
explanation: The face-area ratio is 16 : 1, so the edge ratio is √16 : 1 = 4 : 1. Four small cubes fit in each direction, giving 4³ = 64.
geo36-g142.answerHtml: The face-area ratio is 16 : 1, so the edge ratio is √16 : 1 = 4 : 1. Four small cubes fit in each direction, giving 4³ = 64.

methods.title: Convert area ratio to edge ratio, then volume ratio
steps: The face-area ratio is 16 : 1, so the edge ratio is √16 : 1 = 4 : 1. Four small cubes fit in each direction, giving 4³ = 64.

methods.title: Choose a unit face for the small cube
steps: Let the small face area be 1, so its edge is 1. The large face area is 16, so its edge is 4. The large volume is 64 and the small volume is 1, and the 4×4×4 arrangement fills it without gaps.

geo35-g125.stemHtml: Twelve identical cubes, each with edge 1 cm, are joined face to face to form a rectangular block. Which of the following block dimensions gives the smallest total surface area?
explanation: For dimensions a, b, c, the area is 2(ab + ac + bc). The four areas are 50, 40, 38 and 32 cm² for the listed dimension triples 1×1×12, 1×2×6, 1×3×4 and 2×2×3. The 2×2×3 block has the smallest area.

methods.title: Compare the surface areas of the four blocks
steps: For dimensions a, b, c, the area is 2(ab + ac + bc). The four areas are 50, 40, 38 and 32 cm² for the listed dimension triples 1×1×12, 1×2×6, 1×3×4 and 2×2×3. The 2×2×3 block has the smallest area.

methods.title: Count the faces hidden by contacts
steps: Twelve separate unit cubes have 72 unit faces. Each face-to-face contact hides two faces. The four blocks have 11, 16, 17 and 20 contacts, respectively, leaving 50, 40, 38 and 32 exposed faces. The 2×2×3 block hides the most faces.

methods.title: Count opposite pairs of outside faces
steps: For the 2×2×3 block, two outside faces contain 4 unit squares each and four contain 6 each, giving 8 + 24 = 32. The other three blocks give 2 + 24 + 24 = 50, 4 + 12 + 24 = 40, and 6 + 8 + 24 = 38.

geo35-g126.stem: A cylinder is inscribed in a rectangular box whose square base has side 2a and whose height is 3a. The cylinder has the same height as the box, and its circular bases are inscribed in the square bases. What fraction of the box’s volume lies outside the cylinder?
geo35-g126.stemRich: A cylinder is inscribed in a rectangular box whose square base has side 2a and whose height is 3a. The cylinder has the same height as the box, and its circular bases are inscribed in the square bases. What fraction of the box’s volume lies outside the cylinder?
geo35-g126.stemHtml: A cylinder is inscribed in a rectangular box whose square base has side 2a and whose height is 3a. The cylinder has the same height as the box, and its circular bases are inscribed in the square bases. What fraction of the box’s volume lies outside the cylinder?
explanation: The box volume is $(2a)^2(3a)=12a^3$. The cylinder radius is a, so its volume is $3\pi a^3$. The requested fraction is $\frac{12a^3-3\pi a^3}{12a^3}=1-\frac{\pi}{4}$.

methods.title: Subtract the cylinder volume from the box volume
steps: The box volume is $(2a)^2(3a)=12a^3$. The cylinder radius is a, so its volume is $3\pi a^3$. The requested fraction is $\frac{12a^3-3\pi a^3}{12a^3}=1-\frac{\pi}{4}$.

methods.title: Compare the top-view areas
steps: Both solids have the same height. The circle occupies $\frac{\pi a^2}{4a^2}=\frac{\pi}{4}$ of the square base, so the portion outside it is $1-\frac{\pi}{4}$.

methods.title: Choose a convenient scale and check the choices
steps: Set a = 3. The box volume is 324 and the cylinder volume is 81π. Their unoccupied fraction is $1-\frac{\pi}{4}$. At this value the other three expressions are different.

methods.title: Use scale invariance and positivity
steps: The fraction must stay constant when every length is scaled, so it cannot contain an uncancelled a. Also, a volume fraction is positive here, while $1-\frac{\pi}{2}<0$. These observations leave $1-\frac{\pi}{4}$.

geo35-g127.stem: A pyramid is removed from a cube. The pyramid’s base is the entire bottom face of the cube, and its apex lies on the top face. The remaining solid has volume 54 cm³. What was the volume of the pyramid (in cm³)?
geo35-g127.stemRich: A pyramid is removed from a cube. The pyramid’s base is the entire bottom face of the cube, and its apex lies on the top face. The remaining solid has volume 54 cm³. What was the volume of the pyramid (in cm³)?
geo35-g127.stemHtml: A pyramid is removed from a cube. The pyramid’s base is the entire bottom face of the cube, and its apex lies on the top face. The remaining solid has volume 54 cm³. What was the volume of the pyramid (in cm³)?
explanation: The cube and pyramid have the same base area and perpendicular height. The pyramid is one third of the cube; the remaining part is two thirds. The removed and remaining volumes are in the ratio 1 : 2, so the removed volume is 54 : 2 = 27 cm³.
geo35-g127.answerHtml: The cube and pyramid have the same base area and perpendicular height. The pyramid is one third of the cube; the remaining part is two thirds. The removed and remaining volumes are in the ratio 1 : 2, so the removed volume is 54 : 2 = 27 cm³.

methods.title: Compare the one-third and two-thirds parts
steps: The cube and pyramid have the same base area and perpendicular height. The pyramid is one third of the cube; the remaining part is two thirds. The removed and remaining volumes are in the ratio 1 : 2, so the removed volume is 54 : 2 = 27 cm³.

methods.title: Let the original cube volume be V
steps: $V-\frac V3=54$, so $\frac{2V}{3}=54$ and $V=81$. The removed pyramid is $\frac{81}{3}=27$ cm³.

geo35-g128.stemRich: A pyramid has a square base with side $2\sqrt2$ cm. Each lateral edge is 5 cm. What is the height of the pyramid (in cm)?
geo35-g128.stemHtml: A pyramid has a square base with side cm. Each lateral edge is 5 cm. What is the height of the pyramid (in cm)?
explanation: Equal lateral edges place the apex above the square’s center. The base diagonal is $(2\sqrt2)\sqrt2=4$, so the center-to-vertex distance is 2. The height satisfies $h^2+2^2=5^2$, giving $h=\sqrt{21}$.

methods.title: Use the center-to-vertex right triangle
steps: Equal lateral edges place the apex above the square’s center. The base diagonal is $(2\sqrt2)\sqrt2=4$, so the center-to-vertex distance is 2. The height satisfies $h^2+2^2=5^2$, giving $h=\sqrt{21}$.

methods.title: Compare the height with a lateral edge
steps: The height is a leg in a right triangle whose hypotenuse is a lateral edge of length 5. Thus $0<h<5$. The three incorrect choices exceed 5, while $\sqrt{21}<5$. Only $\sqrt{21}$ can be the height.

geo35-g129.stemRich: The edge of cube ABCDEFGH is $3\sqrt2$ cm. What is the area of triangle BDG (in cm²)?
geo35-g129.stemHtml: The edge of cube ABCDEFGH is cm. What is the area of triangle BDG (in cm²)?
explanation: BD, DG and GB are diagonals of congruent square faces, so all three equal $(3\sqrt2)\sqrt2=6$. The equilateral triangle area is $\frac{6^2\sqrt3}{4}=9\sqrt3$ cm².
geo35-g129.answerHtml: BD, DG and GB are diagonals of congruent square faces, so all three equal . The equilateral triangle area is cm².

methods.title: Recognize an equilateral triangle
steps: BD, DG and GB are diagonals of congruent square faces, so all three equal $(3\sqrt2)\sqrt2=6$. The equilateral triangle area is $\frac{6^2\sqrt3}{4}=9\sqrt3$ cm².

methods.title: Calculate a base and its altitude
steps: BD = 6. Let M be its midpoint and C the bottom vertex below G. Then CM = 3 and CG = $3\sqrt2$. The right triangle GCM gives $GM=\sqrt{9+18}=3\sqrt3$. Thus $\frac12BD\times GM=9\sqrt3$ cm².

explanation: AE = 2. The top-face diagonal is $EG=\sqrt{2^2+2^2}=2\sqrt2$. Since AE is perpendicular to the top face, triangle AEG is right at E. Thus $AG=\sqrt{2^2+(2\sqrt2)^2}=2\sqrt3$. Add the three sides.
geo35-g130.answerHtml: AE = 2. The top-face diagonal is . Since AE is perpendicular to the top face, triangle AEG is right at E. Thus . Add the three sides.

methods.title: Use two right triangles
steps: AE = 2. The top-face diagonal is $EG=\sqrt{2^2+2^2}=2\sqrt2$. Since AE is perpendicular to the top face, triangle AEG is right at E. Thus $AG=\sqrt{2^2+(2\sqrt2)^2}=2\sqrt3$. Add the three sides.

methods.title: Use the cube’s fixed diagonal ratios
steps: For edge s, a face diagonal is $s\sqrt2$ and a body diagonal is $s\sqrt3$. The triangle contains one of each type, so its perimeter is $s(1+\sqrt2+\sqrt3)$. Substitute s = 2.

geo35-g131.stem: Identical cubes with edge 3 cm are placed in a rectangular box with internal dimensions 10 cm × 7 cm × 8 cm. The cube edges must be parallel to the box edges. What is the greatest number of cubes that can fit entirely inside the box?
geo35-g131.stemRich: Identical cubes with edge 3 cm are placed in a rectangular box with internal dimensions 10 cm × 7 cm × 8 cm. The cube edges must be parallel to the box edges. What is the greatest number of cubes that can fit entirely inside the box?
geo35-g131.stemHtml: Identical cubes with edge 3 cm are placed in a rectangular box with internal dimensions 10 cm × 7 cm × 8 cm. The cube edges must be parallel to the box edges. What is the greatest number of cubes that can fit entirely inside the box?
explanation: Along the 10 cm length, 3 cubes fit; along the 7 cm width, 2 fit; along the 8 cm height, 2 fit. Multiply 3 × 2 × 2 = 12. The unused strips cannot accommodate another aligned cube.
geo35-g131.answerHtml: Along the 10 cm length, 3 cubes fit; along the 7 cm width, 2 fit; along the 8 cm height, 2 fit. Multiply 3 × 2 × 2 = 12. The unused strips cannot accommodate another aligned cube.

methods.title: Count complete cubes in each direction
steps: Along the 10 cm length, 3 cubes fit; along the 7 cm width, 2 fit; along the 8 cm height, 2 fit. Multiply 3 × 2 × 2 = 12. The unused strips cannot accommodate another aligned cube.

methods.title: Count a layer, then complete layers
steps: A horizontal layer holds 3 × 2 = 6 cubes and is 3 cm high. Two complete layers use 6 cm of the 8 cm height. A third would need 9 cm, so only 2 layers fit, giving 12 cubes.

geo35-g132.stemHtml: Twenty-seven identical cubes, each with edge 2 cm, form a larger cube. One corner cube is removed, as shown in the accompanying figure. How do the volume and total surface area of the remaining solid change?

The volume decreases by 8 cm³, and the surface area is unchanged.
The volume decreases by 8 cm³, and the surface area decreases by 12 cm².
The volume decreases by 8 cm³, and the surface area increases by 12 cm².

explanation: The removed cube has volume 2³ = 8 cm³. It previously exposed 3 faces, each of area 4 cm². Removing it loses those 3 faces but exposes 3 equal faces of neighboring cubes. The net surface-area change is zero.
geo35-g132.answerHtml: The removed cube has volume 2³ = 8 cm³. It previously exposed 3 faces, each of area 4 cm². Removing it loses those 3 faces but exposes 3 equal faces of neighboring cubes. The net surface-area change is zero.

methods.title: Compare lost and newly exposed faces
steps: The removed cube has volume 2³ = 8 cm³. It previously exposed 3 faces, each of area 4 cm². Removing it loses those 3 faces but exposes 3 equal faces of neighboring cubes. The net surface-area change is zero.

methods.title: Calculate before and after
steps: The original cube has edge 6, volume 216 and surface area 216. The remaining volume is 216 − 8 = 208 cm³. Its surface area is 216 − 12 + 12 = 216 cm².

methods.title: Use a general exposed-face rule
steps: If a removed boundary cube originally has k exposed faces, removing it reveals 6 − k neighboring faces. The change in face count is (6 − k) − k = 6 − 2k. At a corner k = 3, so the change is zero.

geo35-g122.stem: A cone and a cylinder have equal base areas. The volume of the cone is twice the volume of the cylinder. If the cylinder’s height is h, what is the cone’s height?
geo35-g122.stemRich: A cone and a cylinder have equal base areas. The volume of the cone is twice the volume of the cylinder. If the cylinder’s height is h, what is the cone’s height?
geo35-g122.stemHtml: A cone and a cylinder have equal base areas. The volume of the cone is twice the volume of the cylinder. If the cylinder’s height is h, what is the cone’s height?
explanation: Let the common base area be B and the cone height be H. Then $\frac{BH}{3}=2Bh$. Divide by the positive B and multiply by 3 to obtain $H=6h$.
geo35-g122.answerHtml: Let the common base area be B and the cone height be H. Then . Divide by the positive B and multiply by 3 to obtain .

methods.title: Write the two volumes using one base area
steps: Let the common base area be B and the cone height be H. Then $\frac{BH}{3}=2Bh$. Divide by the positive B and multiply by 3 to obtain $H=6h$.

methods.title: Compare with a cone of the same height
steps: With the cylinder’s base area and height h, a cone would have one third of the cylinder’s volume. To reach twice the cylinder’s volume, multiply that cone’s height by 6. Its required height is 6h.

geo35-g123.stem: The volume of rectangular box ABCDEFGH is 216 cm³. M lies on AB, AM : MB = 1 : 2, and N lies directly above M on EF. What is the volume of triangular prism AMD–ENH (in cm³)?
geo35-g123.stemRich: The volume of rectangular box ABCDEFGH is 216 cm³. M lies on AB, AM : MB = 1 : 2, and N lies directly above M on EF. What is the volume of triangular prism AMD–ENH (in cm³)?
geo35-g123.stemHtml: The volume of rectangular box ABCDEFGH is 216 cm³. M lies on AB, AM : MB = 1 : 2, and N lies directly above M on EF. What is the volume of triangular prism AMD–ENH (in cm³)?
explanation: AM is one third of AB. Triangle AMD has half the area of the rectangle with sides AM and AD, so it has one sixth of the box’s base area. The prism and box have the same height. Its volume is therefore 216 : 6 = 36 cm³.
geo35-g123.answerHtml: AM is one third of AB. Triangle AMD has half the area of the rectangle with sides AM and AD, so it has one sixth of the box’s base area. The prism and box have the same height. Its volume is therefore 216 : 6 = 36 cm³.

methods.title: Compare the base areas
steps: AM is one third of AB. Triangle AMD has half the area of the rectangle with sides AM and AD, so it has one sixth of the box’s base area. The prism and box have the same height. Its volume is therefore 216 : 6 = 36 cm³.

methods.title: Use dimensions that cancel
steps: Write AM = x, MB = 2x, AD = y and AE = h. The box volume is $3xyh=216$, so $xyh=72$. The triangular prism volume is $\frac{xyh}{2}=36$ cm³.

methods.title: Split the box into six equal-volume triangular prisms
steps: Divide AB into three equal parts and cut each of the three resulting rectangular bases along a diagonal. The box becomes six triangular prisms with equal base areas and a common height. Each has volume 36 cm³.

geo35-g124.stemRich: The bases of a right triangular prism are right triangles. Each base has a leg of 5 cm and a hypotenuse of 13 cm. The height of the prism is 4 cm. What is its lateral surface area (in cm²)?
geo35-g124.stemHtml: The bases of a right triangular prism are right triangles. Each base has a leg of 5 cm and a hypotenuse of 13 cm. The height of the prism is 4 cm. What is its lateral surface area (in cm²)?
explanation: The missing base leg is 12, since 5² + 12² = 13². The base perimeter is 5 + 12 + 13 = 30. The lateral surface area is 30 × 4 = 120 cm².
geo35-g124.answerHtml: The missing base leg is 12, since 5² + 12² = 13². The base perimeter is 5 + 12 + 13 = 30. The lateral surface area is 30 × 4 = 120 cm².

methods.title: Base perimeter times prism height

methods.title: Add the three rectangular lateral faces
steps: The three faces have areas 5 × 4 = 20, 12 × 4 = 48, and 13 × 4 = 52 cm². Their total is 120 cm². The two triangular bases are excluded.

geo35-core-p01.stem: A rectangle measuring 5 cm × 3 cm is rotated through one full turn about one of its 5 cm sides. What is the volume of the solid formed (in cm³)?
geo35-core-p01.stemRich: A rectangle measuring 5 cm × 3 cm is rotated through one full turn about one of its 5 cm sides. What is the volume of the solid formed (in cm³)?
geo35-core-p01.stemHtml: A rectangle measuring 5 cm × 3 cm is rotated through one full turn about one of its 5 cm sides. What is the volume of the solid formed (in cm³)?
explanation: The axis of rotation becomes the cylinder’s height, 5. The distance from that axis to the opposite rectangle side becomes the radius, 3. The volume is π × 3² × 5 = 45π cm³.
geo35-core-p01.answerHtml: The axis of rotation becomes the cylinder’s height, 5. The distance from that axis to the opposite rectangle side becomes the radius, 3. The volume is π × 3² × 5 = 45π cm³.

methods.title: Identify the cylinder formed by rotation
steps: The axis of rotation becomes the cylinder’s height, 5. The distance from that axis to the opposite rectangle side becomes the radius, 3. The volume is π × 3² × 5 = 45π cm³.

methods.title: Follow the horizontal segments
steps: Each horizontal segment of length 3 sweeps out a disk of radius 3 and area 9π. These equal cross sections extend through height 5, giving 9π × 5 = 45π cm³.

geo35-core-p02.stem: A cone has base radius 2a and height 6a, where a > 0. What is its volume?
geo35-core-p02.stemRich: A cone has base radius 2a and height 6a, where a > 0. What is its volume?
geo35-core-p02.stemHtml: A cone has base radius 2a and height 6a, where a > 0. What is its volume?
explanation: $V=\frac{\pi(2a)^2(6a)}3=\frac{24\pi a^3}3=8\pi a^3$. Square both the 2 and the a in the radius.
geo35-core-p02.answerHtml: . Square both the 2 and the a in the radius.

methods.title: Substitute in the cone formula
steps: $V=\frac{\pi(2a)^2(6a)}3=\frac{24\pi a^3}3=8\pi a^3$. Square both the 2 and the a in the radius.

methods.title: Compare with a cylinder
steps: A cylinder with the same base and height has base area 4πa² and volume 24πa³. The cone occupies one third of that volume, or 8πa³.

geo35-core-p03.stem: A rectangular box has volume 112 cm³. Two of its faces are squares with side 4 cm, and its other four faces are rectangles that are not squares. What is the area of each rectangular face (in cm²)?
geo35-core-p03.stemRich: A rectangular box has volume 112 cm³. Two of its faces are squares with side 4 cm, and its other four faces are rectangles that are not squares. What is the area of each rectangular face (in cm²)?
geo35-core-p03.stemHtml: A rectangular box has volume 112 cm³. Two of its faces are squares with side 4 cm, and its other four faces are rectangles that are not squares. What is the area of each rectangular face (in cm²)?
explanation: The two square faces are opposite. The dimensions are 4, 4 and h, so 16h = 112 and h = 7. Each other face has area 4 × 7 = 28 cm².
geo35-core-p03.answerHtml: The two square faces are opposite. The dimensions are 4, 4 and h, so 16h = 112 and h = 7. Each other face has area 4 × 7 = 28 cm².

methods.title: Find the third dimension
steps: The two square faces are opposite. The dimensions are 4, 4 and h, so 16h = 112 and h = 7. Each other face has area 4 × 7 = 28 cm².

methods.title: Divide volume by the remaining perpendicular edge
steps: Treat one requested rectangular face as the base. The distance to the opposite face is 4. Its area is therefore 112 : 4 = 28 cm²; finding the third edge separately is unnecessary.

explanation: The cone is one third of the cylinder, leaving two thirds. Remaining : removed is therefore 2 : 1.

methods.title: Compare fractional shares

methods.title: Calculate both volumes

geo35-core-p05.stemRich: A cube with edge 2 cm is cut into two congruent triangular prisms by a plane through diagonals of two opposite faces. What is the total surface area of one prism (in cm²)?
geo35-core-p05.stemHtml: A cube with edge 2 cm is cut into two congruent triangular prisms by a plane through diagonals of two opposite faces. What is the total surface area of one prism (in cm²)?
explanation: The two triangular bases together make one 2×2 square, area 4. Two lateral faces are 2×2 squares, total area 8. The cut face is a rectangle with sides 2 and $2\sqrt2$, area $4\sqrt2$. Total: $12+4\sqrt2$.
geo35-core-p05.answerHtml: The two triangular bases together make one 2×2 square, area 4. Two lateral faces are 2×2 squares, total area 8. The cut face is a rectangle with sides 2 and , area . Total: .

methods.title: Add the five faces
steps: The two triangular bases together make one 2×2 square, area 4. Two lateral faces are 2×2 squares, total area 8. The cut face is a rectangle with sides 2 and $2\sqrt2$, area $4\sqrt2$. Total: $12+4\sqrt2$.

methods.title: Take half the old boundary and add the cut face
steps: One half retains half the cube’s original surface area, $24:2=12$. It also gains the rectangular cut face of area $2\times2\sqrt2=4\sqrt2$.

geo35-core-p06.stem: A rectangular box has base ABCD, with AB = 8 cm, AD = 4 cm, and height 5 cm. M lies on AB and N lies on DC, with AM = NC = 3 cm. A prism has base AMND and the same height as the box. What is its volume (in cm³)?
geo35-core-p06.stemRich: A rectangular box has base ABCD, with AB = 8 cm, AD = 4 cm, and height 5 cm. M lies on AB and N lies on DC, with AM = NC = 3 cm. A prism has base AMND and the same height as the box. What is its volume (in cm³)?
geo35-core-p06.stemHtml: A rectangular box has base ABCD, with AB = 8 cm, AD = 4 cm, and height 5 cm. M lies on AB and N lies on DC, with AM = NC = 3 cm. A prism has base AMND and the same height as the box. What is its volume (in cm³)?
explanation: DN = DC − NC = 8 − 3 = 5. The trapezoid base has parallel sides 3 and 5 and height 4, so its area is (3 + 5) × 4 : 2 = 16. Multiply by prism height 5 to get 80.
geo35-core-p06.answerHtml: DN = DC − NC = 8 − 3 = 5. The trapezoid base has parallel sides 3 and 5 and height 4, so its area is (3 + 5) × 4 : 2 = 16. Multiply by prism height 5 to get 80.

methods.title: Use the trapezoid base
steps: DN = DC − NC = 8 − 3 = 5. The trapezoid base has parallel sides 3 and 5 and height 4, so its area is (3 + 5) × 4 : 2 = 16. Multiply by prism height 5 to get 80.

methods.title: Use the half-volume partition
steps: A half-turn about the center of rectangle ABCD exchanges M and N and exchanges the two regions cut by MN. They have equal areas. The prism is half the box volume, so 8 × 4 × 5 : 2 = 80.
