geo35-core-p07.stem: Solid A is formed by joining two pentagonal pyramids along their entire bases. Solid B is a cube. What is the ratio of the number of edges of A to the number of edges of B?
geo35-core-p07.stemRich: Solid A is formed by joining two pentagonal pyramids along their entire bases. Solid B is a cube. What is the ratio of the number of edges of A to the number of edges of B?
geo35-core-p07.stemHtml: Solid A is formed by joining two pentagonal pyramids along their entire bases. Solid B is a cube. What is the ratio of the number of edges of A to the number of edges of B?
explanation: Solid A has 5 edges around the shared pentagon, 5 from the upper apex and 5 from the lower apex, for a total of 15. The cube has 12 edges. The ratio is 15 : 12 = 5 : 4.
geo35-core-p07.answerHtml: Solid A has 5 edges around the shared pentagon, 5 from the upper apex and 5 from the lower apex, for a total of 15. The cube has 12 edges. The ratio is 15 : 12 = 5 : 4.

methods.title: Count the three groups of edges
steps: Solid A has 5 edges around the shared pentagon, 5 from the upper apex and 5 from the lower apex, for a total of 15. The cube has 12 edges. The ratio is 15 : 12 = 5 : 4.

methods.title: Count face-edge incidences
steps: Solid A has 10 triangular outer faces. They contribute 30 face edges, but each actual edge belongs to 2 faces, so there are 15 edges. The cube’s 6 square faces give 24 face edges, hence 12 actual edges. The ratio is 5 : 4.

geo35-core-p08.stemHtml: The base of a rectangular box is square ABCD. M lies on AB with AM = AB : 3, and N lies on DC with DN = 2 DC : 3. Vertical planes through AN and MC divide the box into a middle prism with base AMCN and two outer prisms. What is the ratio of the combined outer volumes to the middle volume?
explanation: The middle base AMCN is a parallelogram. Its base AM is one third of AB and its perpendicular height is AD, so it occupies one third of the square. The outer parts total two thirds. Equal prism heights give volume ratio 2 : 1.
geo35-core-p08.answerHtml: The middle base AMCN is a parallelogram. Its base AM is one third of AB and its perpendicular height is AD, so it occupies one third of the square. The outer parts total two thirds. Equal prism heights give volume ratio 2 : 1.

methods.title: Compare the common-height base regions
steps: The middle base AMCN is a parallelogram. Its base AM is one third of AB and its perpendicular height is AD, so it occupies one third of the square. The outer parts total two thirds. Equal prism heights give volume ratio 2 : 1.

methods.title: Choose a square side of 3
steps: The square area is 9. Each outer triangle has legs 2 and 3, so each has area 3. The middle area is 9 − 3 − 3 = 3. The ratio of outer to middle areas, and volumes, is 6 : 3 = 2 : 1.

explanation: Reducing 9 to 7 gives dimensions 7, 7, 5 and volume 245. Reducing 7 to 5 gives 9, 5, 5 and volume 225. Reducing 9 to 5 gives 5, 7, 5 and volume 175. Any further reduction gives no larger valid block. The maximum is 245.

methods.title: Compare the largest valid reductions
steps: Reducing 9 to 7 gives dimensions 7, 7, 5 and volume 245. Reducing 7 to 5 gives 9, 5, 5 and volume 225. Reducing 9 to 5 gives 5, 7, 5 and volume 175. Any further reduction gives no larger valid block. The maximum is 245.

methods.title: Compare retained fractions
steps: Starting volume is 315. Matching 9 to 7 retains 7 ninths, giving 245. Matching 7 to 5 retains 5 sevenths, giving 225. Since 7 ninths exceeds 5 sevenths, the first retains more. Matching 9 directly to 5 is smaller still.

steps: The product of the adjacent face areas equals the common edge times the box volume. Thus the common edge is $350:140=\frac52$ cm. No separate values for b and c are required.

geo35-core-p13.stemRich: Cylinders with radius 1 cm and height 4 cm are packed upright in a cube with internal edge 12 cm. In each layer, their bases are arranged in straight rows and columns parallel to the cube’s edges. What is the greatest number of cylinders that can fit?
geo35-core-p13.stemHtml: Cylinders with radius 1 cm and height 4 cm are packed upright in a cube with internal edge 12 cm. In each layer, their bases are arranged in straight rows and columns parallel to the cube’s edges. What is the greatest number of cylinders that can fit?
explanation: Each diameter is 2 cm. A layer holds 6 rows of 6 cylinders, or 36. The height permits 12 : 4 = 3 layers. The total is 36 × 3 = 108.
geo35-core-p13.answerHtml: Each diameter is 2 cm. A layer holds 6 rows of 6 cylinders, or 36. The height permits 12 : 4 = 3 layers. The total is 36 × 3 = 108.

methods.title: Count rows, columns and layers
steps: Each diameter is 2 cm. A layer holds 6 rows of 6 cylinders, or 36. The height permits 12 : 4 = 3 layers. The total is 36 × 3 = 108.

methods.title: Construct the small choice and rule out the others by volume
steps: The 6×6×3 arrangement fits 108 cylinders. Each cylinder has volume 4π > 12, so 150 would require more than 1,800 cm³, exceeding the cube’s 1,728 cm³. The larger choices are also impossible. This checks all alternatives without assuming volume alone determines packing.

geo35-core-p14.stem: A cylinder has height 12 cm and base area 9π cm². Two cuts parallel to its bases divide it into three cylinders of equal height. By how much does the sum of their total surface areas exceed the original surface area (in cm²)?
geo35-core-p14.stemRich: A cylinder has height 12 cm and base area 9π cm². Two cuts parallel to its bases divide it into three cylinders of equal height. By how much does the sum of their total surface areas exceed the original surface area (in cm²)?
geo35-core-p14.stemHtml: A cylinder has height 12 cm and base area 9π cm². Two cuts parallel to its bases divide it into three cylinders of equal height. By how much does the sum of their total surface areas exceed the original surface area (in cm²)?
explanation: The curved lateral surface is divided but its total area is unchanged. Each of the two cuts creates two new circular faces, giving four new bases. The increase is 4 × 9π = 36π.
geo35-core-p14.answerHtml: The curved lateral surface is divided but its total area is unchanged. Each of the two cuts creates two new circular faces, giving four new bases. The increase is 4 × 9π = 36π.

methods.title: Count only the new faces
steps: The curved lateral surface is divided but its total area is unchanged. Each of the two cuts creates two new circular faces, giving four new bases. The increase is 4 × 9π = 36π.

methods.title: Calculate before and after
steps: The radius is 3. Original area is 2π×3×12 + 2×9π = 90π. Each new cylinder has height 4 and area 24π + 18π = 42π. Three total 126π, an increase of 36π.

geo35-core-p15.stemRich: A rectangular block of drawing chalk measures 3 cm × 2 cm × $1\frac12$ cm. Each complete day of use removes at least $\frac38$ cm³ of chalk. For how many complete days, at most, can the block last?
geo35-core-p15.stemHtml: A rectangular block of drawing chalk measures 3 cm × 2 cm × cm. Each complete day of use removes at least cm³ of chalk. For how many complete days, at most, can the block last?
explanation: The initial volume is $3\times2\times\frac32=9$ cm³. The longest possible duration uses only $\frac38$ cm³ per day. Thus $9:\frac38=9\times\frac83=24$ days.
geo35-core-p15.answerHtml: The initial volume is cm³. The longest possible duration uses only cm³ per day. Thus days.

methods.title: Use the smallest allowed daily loss
steps: The initial volume is $3\times2\times\frac32=9$ cm³. The longest possible duration uses only $\frac38$ cm³ per day. Thus $9:\frac38=9\times\frac83=24$ days.

methods.title: Write the bound on total use
steps: If the block lasts x complete days, the amount used is at least $\frac38x$ and cannot exceed 9. Hence $\frac38x\le9$, so $x\le24$. Exactly 24 is possible at the minimum daily loss.

geo35-core-p16.stemRich: A right cylinder has radius 3 cm and height 8 cm. A solid is formed by extending a 150° sector of its base through the full height. What is the volume of this solid (in cm³)?
geo35-core-p16.stemHtml: A right cylinder has radius 3 cm and height 8 cm. A solid is formed by extending a 150° sector of its base through the full height. What is the volume of this solid (in cm³)?
explanation: The full cylinder volume is $9\pi\times8=72\pi$. A 150° sector is $\frac{150}{360}=\frac5{12}$ of the base, so the solid volume is $\frac5{12}\times72\pi=30\pi$.
geo35-core-p16.answerHtml: The full cylinder volume is . A 150° sector is of the base, so the solid volume is .

methods.title: Take the same fraction of the cylinder volume
steps: The full cylinder volume is $9\pi\times8=72\pi$. A 150° sector is $\frac{150}{360}=\frac5{12}$ of the base, so the solid volume is $\frac5{12}\times72\pi=30\pi$.

methods.title: Calculate sector area first
steps: The sector area is $\frac5{12}\times9\pi=\frac{15\pi}{4}$. Multiplying by height 8 gives 30π.

methods.title: Use the half-volume bound to check the choices
steps: Since 150° < 180°, the solid is less than half the cylinder, whose volume is 72π. Its volume is below 36π. Only 30π satisfies this bound among the choices.

geo35-core-p22.stemHtml: A cylinder has radius 4 cm and lateral surface area 48π cm². What is its volume (in cm³)?
explanation: The lateral-area equation is 2π×4×h = 48π, so h = 6. The volume is π×4²×6 = 96π.
geo35-core-p22.answerHtml: The lateral-area equation is 2π×4×h = 48π, so h = 6. The volume is π×4²×6 = 96π.

methods.title: Find the height first
steps: The lateral-area equation is 2π×4×h = 48π, so h = 6. The volume is π×4²×6 = 96π.

methods.title: Compare the two formulas
steps: For a cylinder, $\frac{V}{S_{\text{lateral}}}=\frac{\pi r^2h}{2\pi rh}=\frac r2$. With r = 4, volume is numerically twice the lateral area, giving 96π in cubic centimetres.

methods.title: Multiply the three face areas

geo35-core-p24.stemHtml: A cube is painted on all six faces and then cut into 64 congruent small cubes, four along each edge. How many small cubes have paint on exactly two faces?
explanation: A small cube has exactly two painted faces if it lies on an edge but not at a corner. Each of 12 edges has 4 − 2 = 2 such cubes. Total: 24.
geo35-core-p24.answerHtml: A small cube has exactly two painted faces if it lies on an edge but not at a corner. Each of 12 edges has 4 − 2 = 2 such cubes. Total: 24.

methods.title: Count edge cubes excluding corners
steps: A small cube has exactly two painted faces if it lies on an edge but not at a corner. Each of 12 edges has 4 − 2 = 2 such cubes. Total: 24.

methods.title: Remove the corner contributions from edge positions
steps: There are 12×4 = 48 positions counted along the large edges. The 8 corner cubes each appear in 3 of these counts and have three painted faces. Remove all 24 corner occurrences, leaving 24 noncorner edge cubes.

geo35-core-p25.stemRich: What is the greatest possible length of a straight, negligibly thin rod that fits entirely inside a cube with edge 6 cm?
geo35-core-p25.stemHtml: What is the greatest possible length of a straight, negligibly thin rod that fits entirely inside a cube with edge 6 cm?
explanation: The greatest distance between two points in the cube is a body diagonal. Its length is 6√3. A rod along that diagonal fits.
geo35-core-p25.answerHtml: The greatest distance between two points in the cube is a body diagonal. Its length is 6√3. A rod along that diagonal fits.

methods.title: Use the body diagonal
steps: The greatest distance between two points in the cube is a body diagonal. Its length is 6√3. A rod along that diagonal fits.

methods.title: Bound the three perpendicular separations
steps: The endpoint separation in each of three perpendicular directions is at most 6. Thus the squared distance is at most 6²+6²+6² = 108. Opposite vertices attain all three maximum separations, giving √108 = 6√3.

geo35-core-p26.stemHtml: A cone has volume 84π cm³. A cylinder has the same base radius as the cone and twice its height. What is the cylinder’s volume (in cm³)?

geo35-core-p26.answerHtml: A cylinder with the same base and height has three times the cone volume. Doubling that cylinder’s height doubles its volume again. The result is 6×84π = 504π.

methods.title: Use two volume factors

methods.title: Compare formulas
steps: If the cone has radius r and height h, $\frac{\pi r^2h}{3}=84\pi$. The requested cylinder has volume $\pi r^2(2h)$, six times the cone volume, or 504π.

AB is the longest side because it is opposite the obtuse angle; each other side is below 6, so the perimeter is below 18. Only 13.5 survives these bounds. A triangle with sides 3.75,3.75,6 provides an obtuse example with that perimeter.

methods.title: Use lower and upper bounds
steps: The other two sides sum to more than 6, so the perimeter exceeds 12. AB is the longest side because it is opposite the obtuse angle; each other side is below 6, so the perimeter is below 18. Only 13.5 survives these bounds. A triangle with sides 3.75,3.75,6 provides an obtuse example with that perimeter.

methods.title: Construct the surviving case
steps: Take AC=BC=3.75 and AB=6. The altitude to AB has length 2.25, since 3.75²−3²=2.25². In either half-triangle, the side of length 3 is longer than the altitude 2.25, so half of angle C exceeds 45°. Hence C>90°, and the perimeter is 13.5.

methods.title: Build a counterexample

geo31-g035.stemHtml: In the accompanying figure, triangles ABC and ACD are right triangles. The marked lengths are in cm. What is the area of quadrilateral ABCD (in cm²)?
explanation: ABC is a 6–8–10 triangle, so AC=10. ACD has leg 10 and hypotenuse 26, so its other leg is 24. The two areas are 6×8 divided by 2=24 and 10×24 divided by 2=120. Their sum is 144.
geo31-g035.answerHtml: ABC is a 6–8–10 triangle, so AC=10. ACD has leg 10 and hypotenuse 26, so its other leg is 24. The two areas are 6×8 divided by 2=24 and 10×24 divided by 2=120. Their sum is 144.

methods.title: Find the shared side, then add the triangle areas
steps: ABC is a 6–8–10 triangle, so AC=10. ACD has leg 10 and hypotenuse 26, so its other leg is 24. The two areas are 6×8 divided by 2=24 and 10×24 divided by 2=120. Their sum is 144.

methods.title: Work in two-centimetre units
steps: Use a unit of 2 cm. The triangles become 3–4–5 and 5–12–13, with areas 6 and 30 square units. Their total is 36 square units. Each square unit is 4 cm², so the area is 144 cm².

explanation: ABD is a 30°–60°–90° triangle with hypotenuse 12, so BD=6 and AB=6√3. BCD is a 45°–45°–90° triangle with hypotenuse BD=6, so BC=CD=3√2. Add only the four outside sides.

methods.title: Pass through the two special ratios
steps: ABD is a 30°–60°–90° triangle with hypotenuse 12, so BD=6 and AB=6√3. BCD is a 45°–45°–90° triangle with hypotenuse BD=6, so BC=CD=3√2. Add only the four outside sides.

methods.title: Use a ratio, then ordinary Pythagoras
steps: BD is half of AD, so BD=6. In ABD, AB²=144−36=108. In BCD, let each equal leg be t; then 2t²=36 and t=3√2. The outside-side sum is 12+6√3+6√2.

explanation: DE is an altitude and median of the equilateral triangle, so EC=3, BC=6 and DE=3√3. Then AE=5√3. The areas of ABC and DBC are 15√3 and 9√3, leaving 6√3.

methods.title: Subtract the two triangle areas
steps: DE is an altitude and median of the equilateral triangle, so EC=3, BC=6 and DE=3√3. Then AE=5√3. The areas of ABC and DBC are 15√3 and 9√3, leaving 6√3.

methods.title: Use AD as the base of each shaded triangle
steps: The shaded triangles ADB and ADC have base AD=2√3. Their perpendicular heights from B and C to the line AD are BE=EC=3. Each area is 3√3, so the total is 6√3.

methods.title: Subtract heights before calculating areas
steps: ABC and DBC share base BC=6. Their height difference is AE−DE=AD=2√3, so the area difference is half of 6 times 2√3.

geo31-g038.stemHtml: Triangle ABC has area 32 cm². Point D lies on BC, and . What is the difference between the areas of ADC and ABD (in cm²)?
explanation: Let BD=x, DC=3x and the common height be h. The whole area is 4 xh divided by 2=32, so xh=16. The smaller area is 8 and the larger is 24. Their difference is 16.
geo31-g038.answerHtml: Let BD=x, DC=3x and the common height be h. The whole area is 4 xh divided by 2=32, so xh=16. The smaller area is 8 and the larger is 24. Their difference is 16.

methods.title: Write the areas with one height
steps: Let BD=x, DC=3x and the common height be h. The whole area is 4 xh divided by 2=32, so xh=16. The smaller area is 8 and the larger is 24. Their difference is 16.

methods.title: Use the base ratio
steps: The two triangles share a height, so their areas are in the base ratio 1:3. Four area units total 32, making each unit 8. Their difference is two units, or 16.

methods.title: Divide into four equal-area triangles
steps: Divide BC into four equal lengths and join the three division points to A. Each small triangle has the same base and height, so each area is 8. ADC contains three pieces and ABD one, leaving a difference of two pieces.

geo31-g039.stemHtml: Four congruent squares, each with side 3 cm, are arranged as in the accompanying figure. What is the perimeter of AEF minus the perimeter of AFG (in cm)?
explanation: AE is the diagonal of a square of side 6, so AE=6√2. AF has perpendicular components 6 and 3, so AF=3√5. The perimeters are 6√2+3+3√5 and 6+3+3√5. Their difference is 6√2−6.
geo31-g039.answerHtml: AE is the diagonal of a square of side 6, so AE=6√2. AF has perpendicular components 6 and 3, so AF=3√5. The perimeters are 6√2+3+3√5 and 6+3+3√5. Their difference is 6√2−6.

methods.title: Calculate both perimeters
steps: AE is the diagonal of a square of side 6, so AE=6√2. AF has perpendicular components 6 and 3, so AF=3√5. The perimeters are 6√2+3+3√5 and 6+3+3√5. Their difference is 6√2−6.

methods.title: Cancel shared and equal sides first
steps: AF appears in both perimeters, and EF=FG=3. Those lengths cancel, so only AE−AG remains. Since AE=6√2 and AG=6, the difference is 6√2−6.

methods.title: Use the sign as an elimination check
steps: After cancelling AF and equal EF, FG, the difference is the diagonal AE minus the side AG of the large square. A diagonal is longer than a side, so the difference is positive. This rules out the two negative expressions but does not by itself distinguish the two positive ones.

geo31-g040.stemHtml: The accompanying figure shows two equilateral triangles with side lengths a and b, where . The total length of the bold segments is twice the perimeter of the smaller triangle. What is ?
explanation: The bold length is 3b−a, because one segment of length a on the large perimeter is not bold. Twice the small perimeter is 6a. Thus 3b−a=6a, so 3b=7a and a divided by b equals 3 divided by 7.

methods.title: Write the two boundary lengths
steps: The bold length is 3b−a, because one segment of length a on the large perimeter is not bold. Twice the small perimeter is 6a. Thus 3b−a=6a, so 3b=7a and a divided by b equals 3 divided by 7.

methods.title: Test a ratio with convenient lengths

geo31-g014.stem: ABC is an equilateral triangle. Point D lies on BC. Given: \angle DAC=30° and DC=6 cm. What is AB (in cm)?
geo31-g014.stemRich: ABC is an equilateral triangle. Point D lies on BC. Given: $\angle DAC=30°$ and $DC=6$ cm. What is AB (in cm)?
geo31-g014.stemHtml: ABC is an equilateral triangle. Point D lies on BC. Given: and cm. What is AB (in cm)?
explanation: Angle A is 60°, so AD bisects it into two 30° angles. In an equilateral triangle the angle bisector is also a median, so BD=DC=6. Hence BC=12 and AB=12.
geo31-g014.answerHtml: Angle A is 60°, so AD bisects it into two 30° angles. In an equilateral triangle the angle bisector is also a median, so BD=DC=6. Hence BC=12 and AB=12.

methods.title: Use the symmetry line
steps: Angle A is 60°, so AD bisects it into two 30° angles. In an equilateral triangle the angle bisector is also a median, so BD=DC=6. Hence BC=12 and AB=12.

methods.title: Use congruent right halves
steps: The bisector from A divides the equilateral triangle into congruent halves. Their matching base pieces are equal, so the full side is twice DC: 12 cm.

geo31-g015.stemHtml: In triangle ABC, and . Point D lies on AB, and . What is ?
explanation: In ABC, each base angle is (180°−24°) divided by 2, or 78°. In BCD, BC=CD, so angles CBD and BDC are both 78°, leaving angle BCD=24°. Thus ACD=78°−24°=54°.
geo31-g015.answerHtml: In ABC, each base angle is (180°−24°) divided by 2, or 78°. In BCD, BC=CD, so angles CBD and BDC are both 78°, leaving angle BCD=24°. Thus ACD=78°−24°=54°.

steps: In ABC, each base angle is (180°−24°) divided by 2, or 78°. In BCD, BC=CD, so angles CBD and BDC are both 78°, leaving angle BCD=24°. Thus ACD=78°−24°=54°.

methods.title: Use the angle on the straight line at D
steps: Angle BDC is 78° from the smaller isosceles triangle. Angle ADC is its supplement, 102°. In triangle ADC, the other known angle is 24°, so ACD=180°−102°−24°=54°.

geo31-g018.stemHtml: ABC is an equilateral triangle with perimeter 18 cm. Points D and E are the midpoints of AB and BC, respectively. What is the area of quadrilateral ADEC (in cm²)?
explanation: The large triangle has side 6. The small triangle BDE has two sides of length 3 and included angle 60°, so it is equilateral with side 3. Subtract its area from the large area.
geo31-g018.answerHtml: The large triangle has side 6. The small triangle BDE has two sides of length 3 and included angle 60°, so it is equilateral with side 3. Subtract its area from the large area.

methods.title: Subtract the two equilateral areas
steps: The large triangle has side 6. The small triangle BDE has two sides of length 3 and included angle 60°, so it is equilateral with side 3. Subtract its area from the large area.

methods.title: Use the area ratio
steps: BDE has half the side length of ABC, so its area is one quarter of the large area. ADEC is the remaining three quarters. Since ABC has area 9√3, the requested area is 27√3 divided by 4.

methods.title: Test the triangle inequality for each choice

explanation: An altitude that also bisects its starting angle makes the triangle isosceles. It does not force the base to equal the other two sides. For example, a triangle with sides 5, 5 and 6 has this symmetry line but is not equilateral.
geo31-advanced-p01.answerHtml: An altitude that also bisects its starting angle makes the triangle isosceles. It does not force the base to equal the other two sides. For example, a triangle with sides 5, 5 and 6 has this symmetry line but is not equilateral.

methods.title: Identify what the combined line proves
steps: An altitude that also bisects its starting angle makes the triangle isosceles. It does not force the base to equal the other two sides. For example, a triangle with sides 5, 5 and 6 has this symmetry line but is not equilateral.

methods.title: Check why the other descriptions force three equal sides
steps: Two 60° angles force the third to be 60°. In an isosceles triangle, a 60° angle also forces all three angles to be 60°. In the last description, twice half an equal side is that whole side, so the base equals it. Only the altitude-and-bisector condition leaves other isosceles shapes possible.

geo31-advanced-p02.stemHtml: In the accompanying figure, ABC is a right isosceles triangle with cm, and ACD is equilateral. What is the perimeter of quadrilateral ABCD (in cm)?
explanation: The hypotenuse AC of the right isosceles triangle is 4√2. Both outside sides of the equilateral triangle, AD and CD, are therefore 4√2. The boundary is AB+BC+CD+DA=8+8√2. AC lies inside and is not counted.
geo31-advanced-p02.answerHtml: The hypotenuse AC of the right isosceles triangle is 4√2. Both outside sides of the equilateral triangle, AD and CD, are therefore 4√2. The boundary is AB+BC+CD+DA=8+8√2. AC lies inside and is not counted.

methods.title: Find the shared side, then trace the outside
steps: The hypotenuse AC of the right isosceles triangle is 4√2. Both outside sides of the equilateral triangle, AD and CD, are therefore 4√2. The boundary is AB+BC+CD+DA=8+8√2. AC lies inside and is not counted.

methods.title: Add perimeters and remove the shared edge twice
steps: The two triangle perimeters total (8+4√2)+12√2=8+16√2. Their common side AC was counted once in each triangle, but appears nowhere on the outside. Subtract 2×4√2 to obtain 8+8√2.

geo31-advanced-p03.stemHtml: In an isosceles triangle, each equal side is four times as long as the base. What is the ratio of the perimeter to the length of an equal side?
explanation: Let the base be one unit. The other sides are four units each, making a perimeter of nine units. The requested ratio is 9 to 4, or 9 divided by 4.
geo31-advanced-p03.answerHtml: Let the base be one unit. The other sides are four units each, making a perimeter of nine units. The requested ratio is 9 to 4, or 9 divided by 4.

methods.title: Measure everything in base-length units

methods.title: Measure everything in equal-side units
steps: Let an equal side be x. The base is x divided by 4, so the perimeter is 2x+x divided by 4=9x divided by 4. Dividing by the equal side x gives 9 divided by 4.

geo31-advanced-p04.stem: Triangles ABC and ACD are right at B and C, respectively, and have equal areas. Given: AB=9 cm and BC=12 cm. What is CD (in cm)?
geo31-advanced-p04.stemRich: Triangles ABC and ACD are right at B and C, respectively, and have equal areas. Given: $AB=9$ cm and $BC=12$ cm. What is CD (in cm)?
geo31-advanced-p04.stemHtml: Triangles ABC and ACD are right at B and C, respectively, and have equal areas. Given: cm and cm. What is CD (in cm)?
explanation: ABC is a scaled 3–4–5 triangle, so AC=15. Its area is 9×12 divided by 2=54. In ACD the perpendicular legs are AC and CD, so 15×CD divided by 2=54 and CD=36 divided by 5.
geo31-advanced-p04.answerHtml: ABC is a scaled 3–4–5 triangle, so AC=15. Its area is 9×12 divided by 2=54. In ACD the perpendicular legs are AC and CD, so 15×CD divided by 2=54 and CD=36 divided by 5.

methods.title: Find the shared hypotenuse and use the equal areas
steps: ABC is a scaled 3–4–5 triangle, so AC=15. Its area is 9×12 divided by 2=54. In ACD the perpendicular legs are AC and CD, so 15×CD divided by 2=54 and CD=36 divided by 5.

methods.title: Cancel the halves before calculating
steps: Equal areas give AB×BC=AC×CD. Once AC=15 is known, CD=9×12 divided by 15. Cancel a factor of 3 first to get 3×12 divided by 5=36 divided by 5.

geo31-advanced-p05.stemHtml: At each vertex of a triangle, consider the reflex angle consisting of the full turn outside its interior angle. What is the average of these three reflex angles?
explanation: The three full turns total 1080°. Removing the three interior angles removes 180°, leaving 900°. The average is 900° divided by 3=300°.

methods.title: Find their total, then divide by three

methods.title: Use the average interior angle
steps: Every triangle has average interior angle 180° divided by 3=60°. Subtracting each interior angle from 360° therefore produces an average of 360°−60°=300°. The triangle need not be equilateral.

methods.title: Find the whole area first

geo31-advanced-p12.stemHtml: A, E and B lie on one line in that order; D, E and C lie on another. The marked angles at A and C are right angles. Given: , and . What is AB?
explanation: In EBC, the legs 2 and 2√3 give hypotenuse EB=4 and angle BEC=30°. Its vertically opposite angle AED is also 30°. In AED, AD=4√3 is opposite 30°, so AE=4√3×√3=12. Thus AB=12+4=16.
geo31-advanced-p12.answerHtml: In EBC, the legs 2 and 2√3 give hypotenuse EB=4 and angle BEC=30°. Its vertically opposite angle AED is also 30°. In AED, AD=4√3 is opposite 30°, so AE=4√3×√3=12. Thus AB=12+4=16.

methods.title: Recognise the two special right triangles
steps: In EBC, the legs 2 and 2√3 give hypotenuse EB=4 and angle BEC=30°. Its vertically opposite angle AED is also 30°. In AED, AD=4√3 is opposite 30°, so AE=4√3×√3=12. Thus AB=12+4=16.

methods.title: Use Pythagoras and matching angle ratios
steps: EB²=4+12=16, so EB=4. The two right triangles have equal angles at E. The side opposite that angle grows from BC=2 to AD=4√3, a factor of 2√3. The adjacent leg therefore grows from CE=2√3 to AE=12. Add AE and EB.

geo31-advanced-p14.stemRich: Which of the following is necessarily true for every isosceles triangle?
geo31-advanced-p14.stemHtml: Which of the following is necessarily true for every isosceles triangle?
choices: Each equal side is longer than the base
Every altitude is also an angle bisector
The altitude to the base is shorter than an equal side
choicesRich: Each equal side is longer than the base
Every altitude is also an angle bisector
The altitude to the base is shorter than an equal side
choicesHtml: Each equal side is longer than the base
Every altitude is also an angle bisector
The altitude to the base is shorter than an equal side
explanation: The altitude to the base forms two right triangles. In either one, an equal side is the hypotenuse and the altitude is a leg. The hypotenuse is longer, so the stated comparison must hold.
geo31-advanced-p14.answerHtml: The altitude to the base forms two right triangles. In either one, an equal side is the hypotenuse and the altitude is a leg. The hypotenuse is longer, so the stated comparison must hold.

methods.title: Look at one half of the triangle
steps: The altitude to the base forms two right triangles. In either one, an equal side is the hypotenuse and the altitude is a leg. The hypotenuse is longer, so the stated comparison must hold.

methods.title: Use the Pythagorean equation
steps: If an equal side is s, half the base is b and the altitude is h, then h²+b²=s². Since b is positive, h²<s² and h<s. The other statements fail for suitable wide or non-equilateral isosceles triangles.

geo31-advanced-p15.stemRich: A, C and B lie on one line. CE bisects angle ACD, and CF bisects angle DCB. E and F lie on these bisectors. Given: angle CEF is $2t$. Which expression equals angle EFC?
geo31-advanced-p15.stemHtml: A, C and B lie on one line. CE bisects angle ACD, and CF bisects angle DCB. E and F lie on these bisectors. Given: angle CEF is . Which expression equals angle EFC?
explanation: Angles ACD and DCB total 180°. Their halves total 90°, so angle ECF is a right angle. The other two angles in ECF must total 90°. Since one is 2t, the other is 90°−2t.
geo31-advanced-p15.answerHtml: Angles ACD and DCB total 180°. Their halves total 90°, so angle ECF is a right angle. The other two angles in ECF must total 90°. Since one is 2t, the other is 90°−2t.

methods.title: Add the two half-angles at C
steps: Angles ACD and DCB total 180°. Their halves total 90°, so angle ECF is a right angle. The other two angles in ECF must total 90°. Since one is 2t, the other is 90°−2t.

methods.title: Use the perpendicular-bisectors fact
steps: The internal bisectors of two adjacent supplementary angles are perpendicular. Therefore triangle ECF is right at C. Its two acute angles are complementary, giving angle EFC=90°−2t.

geo31-advanced-p16.stem: Two angles of a triangle are α and β. At the third vertex, the reflex angle outside the triangle is divided into three equal angles, each measuring δ. Which expression equals δ?
geo31-advanced-p16.stemRich: Two angles of a triangle are α and β. At the third vertex, the reflex angle outside the triangle is divided into three equal angles, each measuring δ. Which expression equals δ?
geo31-advanced-p16.stemHtml: Two angles of a triangle are α and β. At the third vertex, the reflex angle outside the triangle is divided into three equal angles, each measuring δ. Which expression equals δ?
explanation: The third interior angle is 180°−α−β. Its outside reflex angle is 360°−(180°−α−β)=180°+α+β. Divide this by 3 to get 60°+(α+β) divided by 3.
geo31-advanced-p16.answerHtml: The third interior angle is 180°−α−β. Its outside reflex angle is 360°−(180°−α−β)=180°+α+β. Divide this by 3 to get 60°+(α+β) divided by 3.

methods.title: Subtract the interior angle from a full turn
steps: The third interior angle is 180°−α−β. Its outside reflex angle is 360°−(180°−α−β)=180°+α+β. Divide this by 3 to get 60°+(α+β) divided by 3.

methods.title: Test a valid triangle, then check the rule
steps: For α=80° and β=40°, the third angle is 60°, leaving 300° outside. Each third is 100°. Substituting into the choices leaves only 60°+(α+β) divided by 3. The general full-turn calculation explains why it works for every allowed triangle.

geo31-advanced-p17.stem: ABC is right at A, with AB=8 cm and AC=15 cm. AD is the altitude to BC. What is AD (in cm)?
geo31-advanced-p17.stemRich: ABC is right at A, with $AB=8$ cm and $AC=15$ cm. AD is the altitude to BC. What is AD (in cm)?
geo31-advanced-p17.stemHtml: ABC is right at A, with cm and cm. AD is the altitude to BC. What is AD (in cm)?
explanation: The hypotenuse is 17. Using the legs, the area is 8×15 divided by 2=60. Using BC and AD, it is 17×AD divided by 2. Equating them gives AD=120 divided by 17.
geo31-advanced-p17.answerHtml: The hypotenuse is 17. Using the legs, the area is 8×15 divided by 2=60. Using BC and AD, it is 17×AD divided by 2. Equating them gives AD=120 divided by 17.

methods.title: Calculate the same area using two bases
steps: The hypotenuse is 17. Using the legs, the area is 8×15 divided by 2=60. Using BC and AD, it is 17×AD divided by 2. Equating them gives AD=120 divided by 17.

methods.title: Use the similar right triangles
steps: The small triangle ABD and the whole triangle ABC have equal angles at B and a right angle. Their corresponding sides give AD:AC=AB:BC. Therefore AD=15×8 divided by 17. This is the same altitude formula derived from area.

geo31-advanced-p18.stemRich: The side opposite an obtuse angle of a triangle is 8 cm long. Which of the following could be the sum of the other two side lengths (in cm)?
geo31-advanced-p18.stemHtml: The side opposite an obtuse angle of a triangle is 8 cm long. Which of the following could be the sum of the other two side lengths (in cm)?
explanation: The two other sides must total more than 8 by the triangle inequality. Each is shorter than 8 because it lies opposite a smaller angle, so their sum is less than 16. Only 10 remains. It is attainable: sides 5,5,8 form a triangle, and 8²>5²+5² makes the angle opposite 8 obtuse.
geo31-advanced-p18.answerHtml: The two other sides must total more than 8 by the triangle inequality. Each is shorter than 8 because it lies opposite a smaller angle, so their sum is less than 16. Only 10 remains. It is attainable: sides 5,5,8 form a triangle, and 8²>5²+5² makes the angle opposite 8 obtuse.

methods.title: Find necessary bounds and confirm an example
steps: The two other sides must total more than 8 by the triangle inequality. Each is shorter than 8 because it lies opposite a smaller angle, so their sum is less than 16. Only 10 remains. It is attainable: sides 5,5,8 form a triangle, and 8²>5²+5² makes the angle opposite 8 obtuse.

methods.title: Construct an isosceles example geometrically
steps: Take the other sides as 5 and 5. Half the base is 4, so the altitude is 3. Each half of the apex angle is greater than 45° because its opposite leg 4 exceeds its adjacent leg 3. Thus the apex is obtuse and the sum 10 works. The other choices fail the necessary bounds.

geo31-advanced-p19.stem: One triangle has angles 2p, q and 42°. Another has angles p, 2q and 66°. What is p+q?
geo31-advanced-p19.stemRich: One triangle has angles $2p$, $q$ and 42°. Another has angles $p$, $2q$ and 66°. What is $p+q$?
geo31-advanced-p19.stemHtml: One triangle has angles , and 42°. Another has angles , and 66°. What is ?
explanation: The angle sums give 2p+q=138° and p+2q=114°. Adding gives 3(p+q)=252°, so p+q=84°. This matches the requested sum directly.
geo31-advanced-p19.answerHtml: The angle sums give 2p+q=138° and p+2q=114°. Adding gives 3(p+q)=252°, so p+q=84°. This matches the requested sum directly.

methods.title: Add the two equations without finding p and q separately
steps: The angle sums give 2p+q=138° and p+2q=114°. Adding gives 3(p+q)=252°, so p+q=84°. This matches the requested sum directly.

methods.title: Solve for each angle
steps: Double the second equation to get 2p+4q=228°. Subtract the first equation to get 3q=90°, so q=30°. Then p=114°−60°=54°, giving p+q=84°.

explanation: The two equal base angles are each (180°−2t) divided by 2=90°−t. AD halves the angle at A, so angle BAD=45°−t divided by 2. Alternate angles between the parallel lines give x=angle BAD.

methods.title: Find half a base angle and transfer it
steps: The two equal base angles are each (180°−2t) divided by 2=90°−t. AD halves the angle at A, so angle BAD=45°−t divided by 2. Alternate angles between the parallel lines give x=angle BAD.

methods.title: Express every triangle angle using x
steps: Parallel lines give angle BAD=x. The bisector makes angle BAC=2x, and the equal sides make angle ABC=2x too. The angle sum is 4x+2t=180°, so x=45°−t divided by 2.

methods.title: Use two numerical cases when one leaves a tie
steps: At t=20°, the correct value is 35°. Both 45°−t divided by 2 and 55°−t give 35°, so that example alone cannot decide. At t=24°, the geometric calculation gives 33°, while 55°−t gives 31°. The other choices already failed the first test.

geo31-advanced-p21.stem: A right triangle has perimeter 60 cm and hypotenuse 26 cm. What is its area (in cm²)?
geo31-advanced-p21.stemRich: A right triangle has perimeter 60 cm and hypotenuse 26 cm. What is its area (in cm²)?
geo31-advanced-p21.stemHtml: A right triangle has perimeter 60 cm and hypotenuse 26 cm. What is its area (in cm²)?
explanation: Let the legs be a and b. Their sum is 60−26=34, while a²+b²=26²=676. From (a+b)²=a²+b²+2 ab, we get 1156=676+2 ab, so ab=240. The area is ab divided by 2=120.

methods.title: Recognise a scaled triple and verify uniqueness
steps: The 5–12–13 triple doubled gives legs 10 and 24 and hypotenuse 26. These sum to 60 and have area 120. To see why another pair cannot change the answer, the fixed sum 34 and fixed sum of squares 676 force their product to 240.

geo31-advanced-p24.stem: A triangle has integer side lengths. Two sides are 6 cm and 10 cm. How many possible third-side lengths make the 10 cm side the unique longest side?

geo31-advanced-p24.stemHtml: A triangle has integer side lengths. Two sides are 6 cm and 10 cm. How many possible third-side lengths make the 10 cm side the unique longest side?
explanation: The triangle inequality gives 4<x<16. Requiring 10 to be the unique longest side adds x<10. The integer possibilities are 5,6,7,8 and 9: five values.
geo31-advanced-p24.answerHtml: The triangle inequality gives 4<x<16. Requiring 10 to be the unique longest side adds x<10. The integer possibilities are 5,6,7,8 and 9: five values.

methods.title: Intersect the two restrictions

methods.title: Start with the length-order condition
steps: An integer third side shorter than 10 could be 1 through 9. Values 1 through 4 fail because 6+x does not exceed 10. The remaining five values all form triangles.

explanation: The side ratio is 1:√3:2. If the short leg is s, the difference between hypotenuse 2s and short leg s is s itself. Thus s=7 and the other leg is 7√3. Half their product is 49√3 divided by 2.

steps: The side ratio is 1:√3:2. If the short leg is s, the difference between hypotenuse 2s and short leg s is s itself. Thus s=7 and the other leg is 7√3. Half their product is 49√3 divided by 2.

methods.title: Start with the hypotenuse
steps: If the hypotenuse is h, the shorter leg is h divided by 2. Their difference h divided by 2 is 7, so h=14. Pythagoras gives the other leg √(196−49)=7√3, leading to the same area.

methods.title: Find the open interval

geo31-foundation-p20.stemHtml: A triangle has apex angle p and an exterior angle q at its left base vertex. A line parallel to the base intersects the extension of the right side. The angle r there corresponds to the exterior angle at the right base vertex. Which expression equals r?

vr39-g001.stemHtml: A town reduced bus fares. Passenger numbers rose, but the number of cars entering the town center remained unchanged. Which of the following is necessarily true?
choices: The extra bus passengers had previously travelled by car.
The fare reduction had no effect on anyone’s travel choices.
More people used buses after the fare reduction.
The fare reduction caused drivers to leave their cars at home.
choicesRich: The extra bus passengers had previously travelled by car.
The fare reduction had no effect on anyone’s travel choices.
More people used buses after the fare reduction.
The fare reduction caused drivers to leave their cars at home.
choicesHtml: The extra bus passengers had previously travelled by car.
The fare reduction had no effect on anyone’s travel choices.
More people used buses after the fare reduction.
The fare reduction caused drivers to leave their cars at home.
explanation: The passage directly reports that passenger numbers rose. It gives no information about the previous travel habits of those additional passengers and does not establish the cause of the increase.
vr39-g001.answerHtml: The passage directly reports that passenger numbers rose. It gives no information about the previous travel habits of those additional passengers and does not establish the cause of the increase.

methods.title: Follow the reasoning
steps: The passage directly reports that passenger numbers rose. It gives no information about the previous travel habits of those additional passengers and does not establish the cause of the increase.

methods.title: Check the other choices
steps: “The fare reduction caused drivers to leave their cars at home.” — Car entries did not fall, and the passage does not establish what caused any individual to change behavior.
“The extra bus passengers had previously travelled by car.” — The new passengers might previously have walked, cycled, or not travelled at all.
“The fare reduction had no effect on anyone’s travel choices.” — An unchanged car count does not mean that no individual changed a travel choice.
